questions.answer: Examine my conscience, be sorry for my sins, resolve with God's help not to sin again, confess my sins to the priest, receive absolution, and do the penance. Contrition is "sorrow of the soul and detestation for the sin committed, together with the resolution not to sin again" (CCC 1451). The purpose is to receive God's forgiveness and, with His help, to avoid sin.
options: 1. Examine my conscience. 2. Be sorry for my sins. 3. Confess only the sins I am comfortable telling. 4. Keep my most serious sins to myself. 5. Skip the penance if I am busy.

questions.question: What should you do after Holy Communion?
questions.answer: After Holy Communion I should: 1. Thank Jesus for coming to me. 2. Tell Him how much I love Him. 3. Ask Him to help me. 4. Pray for others.
options: After Holy Communion I should: 1. Leave church right away. 2. Talk to my friends. 3. Think about lunch. 4. Forget about Jesus.
After Holy Communion I should: 1. Thank Jesus for coming to me. 2. Tell Him how much I love Him. 3. Ask Him to help me. 4. Pray for others.
After Holy Communion I should: 1. Thank the priest for coming to me. 2. Tell my friends I love them. 3. Ask them to help me. 4. Chat with others.
After Holy Communion I should: 1. Ask Jesus only for the things I want. 2. Tell Him I am bored. 3. Look around the church. 4. Pray only for myself.
questions.correct: After Holy Communion I should: 1. Thank Jesus for coming to me. 2. Tell Him how much I love Him. 3. Ask Him to help me. 4. Pray for others.

questions.question: Where is Jesus kept in the church?
questions.answer: Jesus in the Holy Eucharist is kept in the tabernacle.
options: Jesus in the Holy Eucharist is kept in the confessional.
Jesus in the Holy Eucharist is kept in the tabernacle.
Jesus in the Holy Eucharist is kept in the holy water font.
Jesus in the Holy Eucharist is kept in the choir loft.
questions.correct: Jesus in the Holy Eucharist is kept in the tabernacle.

questions.question: How do you show respect for Jesus in the tabernacle?
questions.answer: I genuflect toward the tabernacle when I enter or leave the church.
options: I turn my back to the tabernacle when I enter or leave the church.
I genuflect toward the tabernacle when I enter or leave the church.
I clap toward the tabernacle when I enter or leave the church.
I wave at the tabernacle when I enter or leave the church.
questions.correct: I genuflect toward the tabernacle when I enter or leave the church.

questions.question: When must Catholics go to Mass?
questions.answer: Catholics must go to Mass on Sundays and Holy Days of Obligation.
options: Catholics must go to Mass on Sundays and Holy Days of Obligation.
Catholics must go to Mass only on Christmas and Easter.
Catholics must go to Mass only when they feel like it.
Catholics must go to Mass only during Advent and Lent.
questions.correct: Catholics must go to Mass on Sundays and Holy Days of Obligation.

questions.question: True or false: at Mass, we listen to readings from the Bible.
questions.answer: True. The readings are part of the liturgy of the Word (CCC 1346).
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What do Catholics receive in Holy Communion?
questions.answer: In the Eucharist "the body and blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ and, therefore, the whole Christ is truly, really, and substantially contained" (CCC 1374).
options: Only a reminder of Jesus.
A blessed bread that stands for Jesus.
Jesus Christ, truly present in the Eucharist.
The grace of Jesus, but not Jesus Himself.
questions.correct: Jesus Christ, truly present in the Eucharist.

questions.question: True or false: at Mass, the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ while still appearing to be bread and wine.
questions.answer: True. "Appearances" means what we can see, taste, and touch. By the consecration the bread and wine are changed into the Body and Blood of Christ (CCC 1376, 1413).
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What do you say when the minister offers you Holy Communion and says, "The Body of Christ"?
questions.answer: We answer "Amen," which means "yes, it is true!" (CCC 1396).
options: "Thank you."
"And with your spirit."
"Amen."
"Lord, I am not worthy."
questions.correct: "Amen."

questions.question: True or false: the Mass includes both listening to God's word and celebrating the Eucharist.
questions.answer: True. "The liturgy of the Word and liturgy of the Eucharist together form 'one single act of worship'" (CCC 1346).
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What is the tabernacle for?
questions.answer: The tabernacle is for "the reservation of the Eucharist in a worthy place so that it could be brought to the sick and those absent, outside of Mass" (CCC 1379). Christ is truly present in the reserved Eucharist.
options: It holds the holy water used for blessings.
It stores the books of readings for Mass.
It keeps the sacred oils used in the sacraments.
It is where the consecrated hosts are reserved.
questions.correct: It is where the consecrated hosts are reserved.

questions.question: True or false: we should treat the Eucharist with reverence because Jesus is truly present.
questions.answer: True. We express our faith in the real presence "by, among other ways, genuflecting or bowing deeply as a sign of adoration of the Lord" (CCC 1378).
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What is one good way to prepare to receive Holy Communion?
questions.answer: We must prepare ourselves "for so great and so holy a moment," beginning by examining our conscience (CCC 1385). Praying and paying attention during Mass helps us receive Jesus well.
options: Pray and pay attention during Mass.
Receive only on days when I feel emotionally moved.
Arrive in time for Communion and skip the readings.
Plan the rest of my day while waiting in line.
questions.correct: Pray and pay attention during Mass.

questions.question: True or false: after receiving Holy Communion, it is good to take time to pray and thank Jesus.
questions.answer: True. Taking time after Communion to thank Jesus and pray is a good practice.
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: If you are aware that you have committed a mortal sin, what should you ordinarily do before receiving Holy Communion?
questions.answer: "Anyone conscious of a grave sin must receive the sacrament of Reconciliation before coming to communion" (CCC 1385; see also CCC 1457).
options: Receive anyway, as long as I feel sorry.
Receive the Sacrament of Reconciliation first.
Wait a week, then receive.
Receive now and confess the sin at Easter.
questions.correct: Receive the Sacrament of Reconciliation first.

questions.question: According to the opening of the Catechism, why did God freely create man?
questions.answer: "God, infinitely perfect and blessed in himself, in a plan of sheer goodness freely created man to make him share in his own blessed life." (CCC 1)
options: To relieve his own loneliness and need for company
To make him share in his own blessed life
To labor in the world so that God could rest
To prove his power to the angels he had made
questions.correct: To make him share in his own blessed life

questions.question: The Catechism follows a great tradition of building catechesis on four pillars. What are they?
questions.answer: Catechesis rests on "the baptismal profession of faith (the Creed), the sacraments of faith, the life of faith (the Commandments), and the prayer of the believer (the Lord's Prayer)." (CCC 13)
options: Scripture, Tradition, the Magisterium, and the liturgy
Faith, hope, charity, and the seven sacraments
The Creed, the sacraments, the Commandments, and the Lord's Prayer
The Creed, the councils, the saints, and the Rosary
questions.correct: The Creed, the sacraments, the Commandments, and the Lord's Prayer

questions.question: Why, according to the Catechism, is the desire for God written in the human heart?
questions.answer: "The desire for God is written in the human heart, because man is created by God and for God; and God never ceases to draw man to himself." (CCC 27)
options: Because man is created by God and for God
Because every culture teaches religion to its children
Because man naturally fears the forces of nature
Because the mind needs some explanation for the world
questions.correct: Because man is created by God and for God

questions.question: In what sense does the Catechism speak of "proofs" for the existence of God?
questions.answer: They are proofs "not in the sense of proofs in the natural sciences, but rather in the sense of 'converging and convincing arguments,' which allow us to attain certainty about the truth." (CCC 31)
options: As experimental proofs of the kind used in the natural sciences
As private opinions that can never yield real certainty
As converging and convincing arguments that allow certainty about the truth
As revelations given directly to certain chosen saints
questions.correct: As converging and convincing arguments that allow certainty about the truth

questions.question: True or false: The Church teaches that God can be known with certainty from the created world by the natural light of human reason.
questions.answer: The Church "holds and teaches that God, the first principle and last end of all things, can be known with certainty from the created world by the natural light of human reason." (CCC 36)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the Catechism mean by the "divine pedagogy" of Revelation?
questions.answer: Revelation "involves a specific divine pedagogy: God communicates himself to man gradually. He prepares him to welcome by stages the supernatural Revelation" that culminates in Christ. (CCC 53)
options: God reveals everything at once to every generation
God teaches only through the written law of Moses
God communicates himself to man gradually, preparing him by stages
God leaves man to discover him by reason alone
questions.correct: God communicates himself to man gradually, preparing him by stages

questions.question: According to the Catechism, when is any new public revelation to be expected?
questions.answer: "No new public revelation is to be expected before the glorious manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ." Yet Revelation "has not been made completely explicit." (CCC 66)
options: Whenever an ecumenical council is convened
Whenever the Church approves a private revelation
At the beginning of each new age of the Church
None is expected before the glorious manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.correct: None is expected before the glorious manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ

questions.question: What is the role of "private" revelations, even those recognized by the Church?
questions.answer: Private revelations "do not belong, however, to the deposit of faith. It is not their role to improve or complete Christ's definitive Revelation, but to help live more fully by it in a certain period of history." (CCC 67)
options: To help people live more fully by Christ's Revelation in a certain period
To complete what was still lacking in Christ's Revelation
To add new doctrines to the deposit of faith
To correct earlier teaching about the Gospel
questions.correct: To help people live more fully by Christ's Revelation in a certain period

questions.question: What does the Church mean by Tradition, as distinct from Sacred Scripture?
questions.answer: "This living transmission, accomplished in the Holy Spirit, is called Tradition, since it is distinct from Sacred Scripture, though closely connected to it." (CCC 78)
options: Any custom long practiced in a local church
The written decrees issued by the councils
The private opinions of respected theologians
The living transmission of the faith accomplished in the Holy Spirit
questions.correct: The living transmission of the faith accomplished in the Holy Spirit

questions.question: True or false: The Church derives her certainty about all revealed truths from the holy Scriptures alone.
questions.answer: The Church "does not derive her certainty about all revealed truths from the holy Scriptures alone. Both Scripture and Tradition must be accepted and honored with equal sentiments of devotion and reverence." (CCC 82)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: How does the Catechism describe the relationship of the Magisterium to the Word of God?
questions.answer: "This Magisterium is not superior to the Word of God, but is its servant. It teaches only what has been handed on to it." (CCC 86)
options: It stands above the Word of God as its judge
It is independent of the Word of God
It is not superior to the Word of God, but is its servant
It may add new revelations to the Word of God
questions.correct: It is not superior to the Word of God, but is its servant

questions.question: What is the Magisterium doing when it defines a dogma?
questions.answer: The Magisterium defines dogmas "when it proposes, in a form obliging the Christian people to an irrevocable adherence of faith, truths contained in divine Revelation" or truths necessarily connected with them. (CCC 88)
options: Offering a theological opinion the faithful may set aside
Issuing a disciplinary rule that may later be relaxed
Proposing truths in a form obliging an irrevocable adherence of faith
Approving a private revelation for public devotion
questions.correct: Proposing truths in a form obliging an irrevocable adherence of faith

questions.question: To whom has the task of interpreting the Word of God authentically been entrusted?
questions.answer: "The task of interpreting the Word of God authentically has been entrusted solely to the Magisterium of the Church, that is, to the Pope and to the bishops in communion with him." (CCC 100)
options: Each believer reading under the Spirit's personal guidance
Biblical scholars working independently of the Church
Each local pastor for his own parish
The Magisterium: the Pope and the bishops in communion with him
questions.correct: The Magisterium: the Pope and the bishops in communion with him

questions.question: How does the Catechism describe the human authors of Sacred Scripture?
questions.answer: God chose men who "made full use of their own faculties and powers so that... it was as true authors that they consigned to writing whatever he wanted written, and no more." (CCC 106)
options: Passive instruments who wrote down words by dictation
Editors who freely added their own message to God's
Copyists who merely preserved older writings
True authors who made full use of their own faculties and powers
questions.correct: True authors who made full use of their own faculties and powers

questions.question: True or false: The Catechism describes the Christian faith as a "religion of the book."
questions.answer: "The Christian faith is not a 'religion of the book.' Christianity is the religion of the 'Word' of God," a Word "incarnate and living." (CCC 108)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: Which sense of Scripture views realities and events in terms of their eternal significance, leading us toward our true homeland?
questions.answer: In "the anagogical sense (Greek: anagoge, 'leading')" we "view realities and events in terms of their eternal significance, leading us toward our true homeland." (CCC 115, 117)
options: The literal sense
The moral sense
The anagogical sense
The allegorical sense
questions.correct: The anagogical sense

questions.question: How many books does the Church's canon of Scripture include?
questions.answer: The canon "includes 46 books for the Old Testament (45 if we count Jeremiah and Lamentations as one) and 27 for the New." (CCC 120)
options: 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New
46 in the Old Testament and 29 in the New
46 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New
49 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New
questions.correct: 46 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New

questions.question: What does Sacred Scripture call man's response of faith to God, the author of revelation?
questions.answer: "By faith, man completely submits his intellect and his will to God." Scripture calls this human response "the obedience of faith." (CCC 143)
options: The fear of the Lord
The sense of the faithful
The act of contrition
The obedience of faith
questions.correct: The obedience of faith

questions.question: According to the Catechism, who is the most perfect embodiment of the obedience of faith?
questions.answer: "Abraham is the model of such obedience offered us by Sacred Scripture. The Virgin Mary is its most perfect embodiment." (CCC 144)
options: Moses
The Virgin Mary
St. Peter
St. John the Baptist
questions.correct: The Virgin Mary

questions.question: How does the Catechism describe faith in relation to God's action?
questions.answer: "Faith is a gift of God, a supernatural virtue infused by him." Before it can be exercised, man needs "the interior helps of the Holy Spirit." (CCC 153)
options: A natural virtue acquired by repeated practice
A reward God gives in return for good works
A gift of God, a supernatural virtue infused by him
An achievement of the human will alone
questions.correct: A gift of God, a supernatural virtue infused by him

questions.question: What, according to the Catechism, moves us to believe revealed truths?
questions.answer: We believe "because of the authority of God himself who reveals them, who can neither deceive nor be deceived," not because they appear true to natural reason. (CCC 156)
options: That revealed truths appear true in the light of natural reason
The agreement of most people in one's own community
The authority of God who reveals them, who can neither deceive nor be deceived
The strength of one's own religious feelings and experiences
questions.correct: The authority of God who reveals them, who can neither deceive nor be deceived

questions.question: True or false: Faith is more certain than all human knowledge because it is founded on the very word of God, who cannot lie.
questions.answer: "Faith is certain. It is more certain than all human knowledge because it is founded on the very word of God who cannot lie." (CCC 157)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: Why, according to the Catechism, can there never be any real discrepancy between faith and reason?
questions.answer: "Since the same God who reveals mysteries and infuses faith has bestowed the light of reason on the human mind, God cannot deny himself, nor can truth ever contradict truth." (CCC 159)
options: Faith and reason deal with wholly separate truths that never meet
Science has already proven every article of the Christian faith
The same God who reveals mysteries and infuses faith gave man the light of reason
The Church forbids any research that might question the faith
questions.correct: The same God who reveals mysteries and infuses faith gave man the light of reason

questions.question: True or false: Once it has been received, the gift of faith can never be lost.
questions.answer: "Faith is an entirely free gift that God makes to man. We can lose this priceless gift," as St. Paul warned St. Timothy. (CCC 162)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: What does the Catechism say the Apostles' Creed is?
questions.answer: The Apostles' Creed "is rightly considered to be a faithful summary of the apostles' faith. It is the ancient baptismal symbol of the Church of Rome." (CCC 194)
options: The ancient baptismal symbol of the Church of Rome
The creed composed at the Council of Nicaea in 325
A creed composed by St. Athanasius of Alexandria
A creed written by Pope Paul VI in 1968
questions.correct: The ancient baptismal symbol of the Church of Rome

questions.question: When God called Moses from the burning bush, what name did he reveal?
questions.answer: In revealing "his mysterious name, YHWH ('I AM HE WHO IS,' 'I AM WHO AM' or 'I AM WHO I AM'), God says who he is and by what name he is to be called." (CCC 205, 206)
options: The Holy One of Israel
The LORD of hosts
God Most High
I AM WHO I AM
questions.correct: I AM WHO I AM

questions.question: Out of respect for God's holiness, how do the people of Israel render the revealed name YHWH when reading Scripture?
questions.answer: "Out of respect for the holiness of God, the people of Israel do not pronounce his name." YHWH is replaced by "the divine title 'LORD' (in Hebrew Adonai, in Greek Kyrios)." (CCC 209)
options: By the title "Messiah" (in Greek, Christos)
By the title "LORD" (Adonai; in Greek, Kyrios)
By the title "Father" (in Aramaic, Abba)
By the title "Emmanuel" (God with us)
questions.correct: By the title "LORD" (Adonai; in Greek, Kyrios)

questions.question: True or false: According to the Catechism, God himself is an eternal exchange of love, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and he has destined us to share in that exchange.
questions.answer: St. John affirms that "God is love": "God himself is an eternal exchange of love, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and he has destined us to share in that exchange." (CCC 221)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the Catechism call the central mystery of Christian faith and life?
questions.answer: "The mystery of the Most Holy Trinity is the central mystery of Christian faith and life. It is the mystery of God in himself." (CCC 234)
options: The mystery of the Incarnation
The mystery of the Eucharist
The mystery of creation
The mystery of the Most Holy Trinity
questions.correct: The mystery of the Most Holy Trinity

questions.question: What does the Catechism teach about God and the human distinction between the sexes?
questions.answer: "God transcends the human distinction between the sexes. He is neither man nor woman: he is God." He "is pure spirit in which there is no place for the difference between the sexes." (CCC 239, 370)
options: God is properly male, as the title "Father" shows
God is both male and female in equal measure
God transcends it: he is neither man nor woman, he is God
God was revealed as female in the Old Testament
questions.correct: God transcends it: he is neither man nor woman, he is God

questions.question: At Nicaea (325) the Church confessed that the Son is "consubstantial" with the Father. What does this mean?
questions.answer: The Church confessed at Nicaea "that the Son is 'consubstantial' with the Father, that is, one only God with him." (CCC 242)
options: That he is the first and greatest creature the Father made
That he became God's Son at his baptism in the Jordan
That he is one only God with the Father
That his substance is similar to, but distinct from, the Father's
questions.correct: That he is one only God with the Father

questions.question: True or false: The filioque ("and the Son") appeared in the Creed confessed at the Council of Constantinople in 381.
questions.answer: "The affirmation of the filioque does not appear in the Creed confessed in 381 at Constantinople." It was gradually admitted into the Latin liturgy between the eighth and eleventh centuries. (CCC 247)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: How do the three divine persons possess the one divinity?
questions.answer: "The divine persons do not share the one divinity among themselves but each of them is God whole and entire." (CCC 253)
options: Each of them possesses one third of the divinity
Only the Father is God in the full sense
Each of them is God whole and entire
They share it by acting at different times in history
questions.correct: Each of them is God whole and entire

questions.question: Of all the divine attributes, which one alone is named in the Creed?
questions.answer: "Of all the divine attributes, only God's omnipotence is named in the Creed: to confess this power has great bearing on our lives." (CCC 268)
options: God's eternity
God's omnipotence
God's mercy
God's omniscience
questions.correct: God's omnipotence

questions.question: Which view, rejected by Christian faith, holds that God made the world like a watchmaker who then abandons it to itself?
questions.answer: "Some admit that the world was made by God, but as by a watchmaker who, once he has made a watch, abandons it to itself (Deism)." (CCC 285)
options: Deism
Pantheism
Dualism
Materialism
questions.correct: Deism

questions.question: As quoted in the Catechism, why did God create all things, according to St. Bonaventure?
questions.answer: God created all things "not to increase his glory, but to show it forth and to communicate it," for God has no other reason for creating "than his love and goodness." (CCC 293)
options: Not to increase his glory, but to show it forth and to communicate it
To increase his own glory and his own happiness
To complete something lacking in his own perfection
Because creation had to flow from him by necessity
questions.correct: Not to increase his glory, but to show it forth and to communicate it

questions.question: What does the Church believe about how God creates?
questions.answer: "God needs no pre-existent thing or any help in order to create, nor is creation any sort of necessary emanation from the divine substance. God creates freely 'out of nothing.'" (CCC 296, 317)
options: From pre-existent matter, as an artisan shapes his material
As a necessary emanation from the divine substance
Through angels who fashioned the material world for him
Freely and out of nothing, needing no pre-existent thing or help
questions.correct: Freely and out of nothing, needing no pre-existent thing or help

questions.question: What does the Church call the dispositions by which God guides his creation toward its ultimate perfection?
questions.answer: "We call 'divine providence' the dispositions by which God guides his creation toward this perfection," since the universe was created "in a state of journeying." (CCC 302)
options: Divine providence
Natural law
Original justice
Blind fate
questions.correct: Divine providence

questions.question: True or false: The Catechism teaches that, as long as creation has not reached perfection, physical evil exists alongside physical good.
questions.answer: God freely willed a world "in a state of journeying" toward perfection: "With physical good there exists also physical evil as long as creation has not reached perfection." (CCC 310)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What is God's relation to moral evil, according to the Catechism?
questions.answer: "God is in no way, directly or indirectly, the cause of moral evil. He permits it, however, because he respects the freedom of his creatures and, mysteriously, knows how to derive good from it." (CCC 311)
options: He directly causes it in order to test his creatures
He causes it indirectly through the laws of nature
He would prevent it but lacks the power to do so
He is in no way its cause, but permits it, respecting creatures' freedom
questions.correct: He is in no way its cause, but permits it, respecting creatures' freedom

questions.question: According to St. Augustine, quoted in the Catechism, what does the word "angel" name?
questions.answer: St. Augustine says: "'Angel' is the name of their office, not of their nature. If you seek the name of their nature, it is 'spirit'." (CCC 329)
options: Their nature, while "spirit" names their office
Their rank within the heavenly choirs
Their dwelling place within heaven
Their office, while "spirit" names their nature
questions.correct: Their office, while "spirit" names their nature

questions.question: True or false: The Catechism teaches that from its beginning until death, human life is surrounded by the watchful care and intercession of angels.
questions.answer: "From its beginning until death, human life is surrounded by their watchful care and intercession." "Beside each believer stands an angel as protector and shepherd leading him to life." (CCC 336)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the "eighth day" signify in the Catechism's teaching on creation?
questions.answer: "For us a new day has dawned: the day of Christ's Resurrection. The seventh day completes the first creation. The eighth day begins the new creation." (CCC 349)
options: The day God rested after the six days of creation
The day of Christ's Resurrection, which begins the new creation
The day of the Last Judgment at the end of time
The day on which God created the first man
questions.correct: The day of Christ's Resurrection, which begins the new creation

questions.question: What does the Catechism say sets man apart among the creatures on earth?
questions.answer: Man is "the only creature on earth that God has willed for its own sake," and "he alone is called to share, by knowledge and love, in God's own life." (CCC 356)
options: He is the only creature that does not depend on any other creature
He is the only creature on earth that God has willed for its own sake
He is the only creature that God keeps in existence
He is the only creature that God declared to be good
questions.correct: He is the only creature on earth that God has willed for its own sake

questions.question: The Church teaches that the soul is the "form" of the body. What does this mean?
questions.answer: "It is because of its spiritual soul that the body made of matter becomes a living, human body; spirit and matter, in man, are not two natures united, but rather their union forms a single nature." (CCC 365)
options: The soul is a separate being temporarily housed in the body
The soul is the outward shape or outline of the body
The soul is produced by the body's own material processes
Through the spiritual soul, the body of matter becomes a living, human body
questions.correct: Through the spiritual soul, the body of matter becomes a living, human body

questions.question: How has God willed man and woman, according to the Catechism?
questions.answer: God willed them "on the one hand, in perfect equality as human persons; on the other, in their respective beings as man and woman," not leaving them "half-made and incomplete." (CCC 369, 372)
options: In perfect equality as persons, and in their respective beings as man and woman
With the man holding greater dignity as the first to be created
As interchangeable beings with no real difference between them
As incomplete halves that God left unfinished
questions.correct: In perfect equality as persons, and in their respective beings as man and woman

questions.question: True or false: The Church teaches that each person's spiritual soul is produced by his or her parents.
questions.answer: "The doctrine of the faith affirms that the spiritual and immortal soul is created immediately by God." (CCC 382)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: What does the Church teach about the origin of the devil?
questions.answer: "The devil and the other demons were indeed created naturally good by God, but they became evil by their own doing." (CCC 391)
options: He is an eternal principle of evil, equal and opposed to God
He was created evil by God in order to test mankind
He is only a symbol of human evil, not a real being
He was created good by God but became evil by his own doing
questions.correct: He was created good by God but became evil by his own doing

questions.question: Why is the sin of the fallen angels unforgivable?
questions.answer: "It is the irrevocable character of their choice, and not a defect in the infinite divine mercy, that makes the angels' sin unforgivable." (CCC 393)
options: Because of a limit in God's mercy toward spiritual beings
Because their sins outnumber those of all humanity
Because of the irrevocable character of their choice
Because God created them without free will
questions.correct: Because of the irrevocable character of their choice

questions.question: According to the Catechism, what did man's first sin consist of?
questions.answer: "Man, tempted by the devil, let his trust in his Creator die in his heart and, abusing his freedom, disobeyed God's command. This is what man's first sin consisted of." (CCC 397)
options: The marital union of Adam and Eve in the garden
Letting trust in his Creator die and, abusing his freedom, disobeying God
Eating a fruit that was poisonous by its nature
Refusing to tend the garden as God had asked
questions.correct: Letting trust in his Creator die and, abusing his freedom, disobeying God

questions.question: Why is original sin called "sin" only in an analogical sense?
questions.answer: "Original sin is called 'sin' only in an analogical sense: it is a sin 'contracted' and not 'committed'"; it is "a state and not an act." (CCC 404)
options: It is not a real condition, only a figure of speech
It is a sin "contracted" and not "committed", a state and not an act
It is committed by each person on reaching the age of reason
It is incurred by imitating the bad example of others
questions.correct: It is a sin "contracted" and not "committed", a state and not an act

questions.question: What does the Catechism teach about human nature after original sin?
questions.answer: "Human nature has not been totally corrupted: it is wounded in the natural powers proper to it" and "inclined to sin." After Baptism, the consequences "persist in man and summon him to spiritual battle." (CCC 405)
options: It is totally corrupted, and its freedom is destroyed
It is unharmed, since Adam only set a bad example
It is fully restored, with no lasting effects, by Baptism
It is not totally corrupted, but wounded and inclined to sin
questions.correct: It is not totally corrupted, but wounded and inclined to sin

questions.question: What is the Genesis passage called that first announces the Messiah and Redeemer, a battle between the serpent and the Woman, and the final victory of her descendant?
questions.answer: "This passage in Genesis is called the Protoevangelium ('first gospel'): the first announcement of the Messiah and Redeemer." (CCC 410)
options: The Protoevangelium
The Shema
The Magnificat
The Exultet
questions.correct: The Protoevangelium

questions.question: What does the name "Jesus" mean in Hebrew?
questions.answer: "Jesus means in Hebrew: 'God saves.'" The name given by the angel Gabriel "expresses both his identity and his mission." (CCC 430)
options: God saves
God is with us
The anointed one
God is gracious
questions.correct: God saves

questions.question: In what threefold office did Jesus fulfill the messianic hope of Israel?
questions.answer: In Israel kings, priests and, in rare instances, prophets were anointed. "Jesus fulfilled the messianic hope of Israel in his threefold office of priest, prophet, and king." (CCC 436)
options: Teacher, healer, and judge
Shepherd, servant, and lawgiver
Priest, prophet, and king
Rabbi, healer, and king
questions.correct: Priest, prophet, and king

questions.question: According to the Catechism, what does it mean to confess or invoke Jesus as "Lord"?
questions.answer: "The title 'Lord' indicates divine sovereignty. To confess or invoke Jesus as Lord is to believe in his divinity." (CCC 455)
options: To honor him as a great human teacher
To accept him as Israel's political ruler
To believe in his divinity
To recognize him as the greatest of the angels
questions.correct: To believe in his divinity

questions.question: True or false: The Incarnation means that Jesus Christ is part God and part man.
questions.answer: False. The Incarnation "does not mean that Jesus Christ is part God and part man.... He became truly man while remaining truly God." (CCC 464)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: What did the Nestorian heresy hold about Christ?
questions.answer: "The Nestorian heresy regarded Christ as a human person joined to the divine person of God's Son." The Council of Ephesus (431) opposed it. (CCC 466)
options: That he was a human person joined to the divine person of God's Son
That he only appeared to have a real human body
That his human nature ceased to exist when the Son assumed it
That the Son of God came to be from things that were not
questions.correct: That he was a human person joined to the divine person of God's Son

questions.question: How did the Council of Chalcedon (451) say that Christ is to be acknowledged in his two natures?
questions.answer: Chalcedon confessed "one and the same Christ, Lord, and only-begotten Son" in "two natures without confusion, change, division, or separation." (CCC 467)
options: Without confusion, change, division, or separation
Blended together into a single new nature
With the human nature absorbed into the divine
Joined only by the agreement of two persons
questions.correct: Without confusion, change, division, or separation

questions.question: What did the Third Council of Constantinople (681) confess about Christ's will?
questions.answer: Christ "possesses two wills and two natural operations, divine and human. They are not opposed to each other, but cooperate." (CCC 475)
options: He has two wills, divine and human, which are not opposed but cooperate
He has only a divine will, which directly moves his human body
He has one will formed by blending the divine and the human
He has two wills, divine and human, which often oppose each other
questions.correct: He has two wills, divine and human, which are not opposed but cooperate

questions.question: True or false: Because Christ's body was finite, his human face can be portrayed, and the Church has recognized holy images of him as legitimate.
questions.answer: True. "The human face of Jesus can be portrayed; at the seventh ecumenical council (Nicaea II in 787) the Church recognized its representation in holy images to be legitimate." (CCC 476)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the dogma of the Immaculate Conception confess?
questions.answer: As Pope Pius IX proclaimed in 1854, Mary "was, from the first moment of her conception... preserved immune from all stain of original sin." (CCC 491)
options: That Jesus was conceived in Mary's womb without a human father
That Mary was taken up body and soul into heavenly glory
That Mary was cleansed of original sin at the Annunciation
That Mary was preserved from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception
questions.correct: That Mary was preserved from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception

questions.question: True or false: Mary's unique holiness comes wholly from Christ, for she was redeemed in a more exalted fashion by reason of her Son's merits.
questions.answer: True. Mary's holiness "comes wholly from Christ: she is 'redeemed, in a more exalted fashion, by reason of the merits of her Son.'" (CCC 492)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: Why does the Church confess that Mary is truly "Mother of God" (Theotokos)?
questions.answer: The one she conceived "was none other than the Father's eternal Son, the second person of the Holy Trinity. Hence the Church confesses that Mary is truly 'Mother of God' (Theotokos)." (CCC 495)
options: Because she gave the eternal Word his divine nature and his divinity
Because she was preserved from original sin from her conception
Because she was taken up body and soul into the glory of heaven
Because the one she conceived as man is the Father's eternal Son, the second person of the Trinity
questions.correct: Because the one she conceived as man is the Father's eternal Son, the second person of the Trinity

questions.question: The liturgy celebrates Mary as "Aeiparthenos." What does this title mean?
questions.answer: The Church confesses "Mary's real and perpetual virginity," and "the liturgy of the Church celebrates Mary as Aeiparthenos, the 'Ever-virgin.'" (CCC 499)
options: Mother of God
Ever-virgin
Full of grace
Seat of Wisdom
questions.correct: Ever-virgin

questions.question: How does the Church understand the Gospel passages that mention "brothers" of Jesus, such as James and Joseph?
questions.answer: The Church understands these passages "as not referring to other children of the Virgin Mary." James and Joseph "are the sons of another Mary" and "are close relations of Jesus." (CCC 500)
options: They are younger children of Mary and Joseph
They are disciples called brothers only in faith
They are close relations of Jesus, the sons of another Mary
They are sons of Zechariah and Elizabeth
questions.correct: They are close relations of Jesus, the sons of another Mary

questions.question: Besides the adoration of Jesus by the magi, what does the great feast of Epiphany celebrate?
questions.answer: "The great feast of Epiphany celebrates the adoration of Jesus by the wise men (magi) from the East, together with his baptism in the Jordan and the wedding feast at Cana in Galilee." (CCC 528)
options: His presentation and his finding in the Temple
His baptism in the Jordan and the wedding feast at Cana
His circumcision and the flight into Egypt
His Transfiguration and his entry into Jerusalem
questions.correct: His baptism in the Jordan and the wedding feast at Cana

questions.question: What was Jesus' baptism by John, on Jesus' part?
questions.answer: "The baptism of Jesus is on his part the acceptance and inauguration of his mission as God's suffering Servant." He "allows himself to be numbered among sinners." (CCC 536)
options: An act of repentance for sins he had personally committed
His ordination as a priest by the last of the prophets
The acceptance and inauguration of his mission as God's suffering Servant
The moment at which he first became the Son of God
questions.correct: The acceptance and inauguration of his mission as God's suffering Servant

questions.question: According to the Catechism, what does the power to "bind and loose" connote?
questions.answer: "The power to 'bind and loose' connotes the authority to absolve sins, to pronounce doctrinal judgments, and to make disciplinary decisions in the Church." (CCC 553)
options: Power to work miracles and to cast out demons in Christ's name
Authority to crown and to depose the rulers of the nations
Power to decide who is predestined to heaven or to hell
Authority to absolve sins, pronounce doctrinal judgments, and make disciplinary decisions
questions.correct: Authority to absolve sins, pronounce doctrinal judgments, and make disciplinary decisions

questions.question: True or false: The Church teaches that all the Jews of Jesus' time, and Jews today, are responsible for the crimes committed during his Passion.
questions.answer: False. "[N]either all Jews indiscriminately at that time, nor Jews today, can be charged with the crimes committed during his Passion." (CCC 597)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: Whom does the Church name as "the authors and the ministers of all the sufferings" that Christ endured?
questions.answer: The Church has never forgotten that "sinners were the authors and the ministers of all the sufferings that the divine Redeemer endured," and imputes to Christians "the gravest responsibility." (CCC 598)
options: The Jewish people as a whole
The Roman soldiers alone
Demons acting without human cooperation
Sinners
questions.correct: Sinners

questions.question: For whom does the Church teach that Christ died?
questions.answer: "The Church, following the apostles, teaches that Christ died for all men without exception": "There is not... a single human being for whom Christ did not suffer." (CCC 605)
options: Only for those predestined to be saved
Only for the people of Israel
For all men without exception
Only for those who would be baptized
questions.correct: For all men without exception

questions.question: True or false: While Christ lay in the tomb, his body underwent decay like any other corpse.
questions.answer: False. Because the Son remained united with his body, "divine power preserved Christ's body from corruption." (CCC 627)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: According to the Catechism, why did Jesus descend into hell, the realm of the dead?
questions.answer: "Jesus did not descend into hell to deliver the damned, nor to destroy the hell of damnation, but to free the just who had gone before him." (CCC 633)
options: To deliver the damned from their punishment
To destroy the hell of damnation
To suffer the punishment due to the damned
To free the just who had gone before him
questions.correct: To free the just who had gone before him

questions.question: Why does the Catechism reject the idea that the Resurrection was produced by the apostles' faith or credulity?
questions.answer: The disciples were "demoralized" and doubtful; "their faith in the Resurrection was born, under the action of divine grace, from their direct experience of the reality of the risen Jesus." (CCC 643, 644)
options: The apostles were too uneducated to invent and spread such a story
Roman officials publicly confirmed the Resurrection in their records
The disciples had fully expected the Resurrection from the very start
The disciples were demoralized and doubting; their faith came from directly encountering the risen Jesus
questions.correct: The disciples were demoralized and doubting; their faith came from directly encountering the risen Jesus

questions.question: How did Christ's Resurrection differ from his raising of Lazarus?
questions.answer: Those Jesus raised "returned by Jesus' power to ordinary earthly life" and would die again. "In his risen body he passes from the state of death to another life beyond time and space." (CCC 646)
options: Christ returned to ordinary earthly life; Lazarus was raised in a glorious body
Christ rose only in spirit; Lazarus rose in his physical body
There was no essential difference, since both of them would die again
Christ passed to another life beyond time and space; Lazarus returned to ordinary earthly life
questions.correct: Christ passed to another life beyond time and space; Lazarus returned to ordinary earthly life

questions.question: What does the Catechism say is meant by "the Father's right hand," where Christ is seated?
questions.answer: "By 'the Father's right hand' we understand the glory and honor of divinity," where the Son "is seated bodily after he became incarnate and his flesh was glorified." (CCC 663)
options: A place of honor just below God, like that of the highest angel
The throne of David in the earthly city of Jerusalem
The resting place of the souls of the just before Christ
The glory and honor of divinity
questions.correct: The glory and honor of divinity

questions.question: What has the Church rejected under the name of "millenarianism"?
questions.answer: The Antichrist's deception takes shape whenever "the claim is made to realize within history that messianic hope which can only be realized beyond history." The Church rejects this "under the name of millenarianism." (CCC 676)
options: The belief that Christ will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead
The custom of praying "Marana tha" to hasten the Lord's return
The teaching that the Church must pass through a final trial before the end
The claim to realize within history the messianic hope that can only be realized beyond history
questions.correct: The claim to realize within history the messianic hope that can only be realized beyond history

questions.question: True or false: The kingdom of God will be fulfilled by a historic triumph of the Church through her progressive ascendancy in the world.
questions.answer: False. "The kingdom will be fulfilled, then, not by a historic triumph of the Church through a progressive ascendancy, but only by God's victory over the final unleashing of evil." (CCC 677)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: True or false: Although the Holy Spirit is the first to awaken faith in us, he is the last of the persons of the Holy Trinity to be revealed.
questions.answer: True. The Holy Spirit "is the first to awaken faith in us," "but the Spirit is the last of the persons of the Holy Trinity to be revealed." (CCC 684)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: The word "Spirit" translates the Hebrew word ruah. What does ruah mean in its primary sense?
questions.answer: "The term 'Spirit' translates the Hebrew word ruah, which, in its primary sense, means breath, air, wind." (CCC 691)
options: Fire, flame, light
Water, spring, river
Breath, air, wind
Oil, anointing, seal
questions.correct: Breath, air, wind

questions.question: What does "Paraclete," Jesus' title for the Holy Spirit, literally mean?
questions.answer: Jesus calls him the "Paraclete," literally, "he who is called to one's side," ad-vocatus. It is commonly translated "consoler." (CCC 692)
options: He who proceeds from the Father
He who speaks through the prophets
He who searches the depths of God
He who is called to one's side
questions.correct: He who is called to one's side

questions.question: Which symbol of the Holy Spirit signifies "the transforming energy of the Holy Spirit's actions"?
questions.answer: "While water signifies birth and the fruitfulness of life given in the Holy Spirit, fire symbolizes the transforming energy of the Holy Spirit's actions." (CCC 696)
options: Water
The dove
Fire
The seal
questions.correct: Fire

questions.question: The image of the seal has been used to express the indelible "character" imprinted by which three sacraments?
questions.answer: The seal "indicates the indelible effect of the anointing with the Holy Spirit in the sacraments of Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders," these "three unrepeatable sacraments." (CCC 698)
options: Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders
Baptism, Confirmation, and the Eucharist
Baptism, Matrimony, and Holy Orders
Confirmation, Penance, and Anointing of the Sick
questions.correct: Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders

questions.question: Because we are dead or at least wounded through sin, what is the first effect of the gift of love?
questions.answer: "Because we are dead or at least wounded through sin, the first effect of the gift of love is the forgiveness of our sins." (CCC 734)
options: Freedom from every temptation
The gift of speaking in tongues
The forgiveness of our sins
The power to work miracles
questions.correct: The forgiveness of our sins

questions.question: Quoting St. Paul, the Catechism names "the fruit of the Spirit." Which list belongs to it?
questions.answer: The Spirit makes us bear "the fruit of the Spirit:... love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control." (CCC 736)
options: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness
Wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge
Prudence, justice, fortitude, and temperance
Poverty, chastity, and obedience
questions.correct: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness

questions.question: What does the word "Church" (Latin ecclesia, from the Greek ek-kalein, "to call out of") mean?
questions.answer: The word "Church" "means a convocation or an assembly. It designates the assemblies of the people, usually for a religious purpose." (CCC 751)
options: A building set apart for worship
The clergy as distinct from the laity
A sacred covenant or agreement
A convocation or an assembly
questions.correct: A convocation or an assembly

questions.question: According to the Catechism, what symbolizes the origin and growth of the Church?
questions.answer: "The origin and growth of the Church are symbolized by the blood and water which flowed from the open side of the crucified Jesus." (CCC 766)
options: The veil of the Temple that was torn in two at Jesus' death
The stone that was rolled away from the empty tomb
The blood and water that flowed from the open side of the crucified Jesus
The twelve baskets of bread left after the multiplication
questions.correct: The blood and water that flowed from the open side of the crucified Jesus

questions.question: In what sense does the Catechism say the Church is "like a sacrament"?
questions.answer: "The Church, in Christ, is like a sacrament—a sign and instrument, that is, of communion with God and of unity among all men." (CCC 775)
options: She is an eighth sacrament, added alongside the seven sacraments
She is a sign only, with no power to bring about what she signifies
She is a sign and instrument of communion with God and of unity among all men
She is a society that represents believers before civil governments
questions.correct: She is a sign and instrument of communion with God and of unity among all men

questions.question: How does one become a member of the People of God?
questions.answer: "One becomes a member of this people not by a physical birth, but by being 'born anew,' a birth 'of water and the Spirit,' that is, by faith in Christ, and Baptism." (CCC 782)
options: By physical descent from Abraham and the twelve tribes of Israel
By being born anew of water and the Spirit, through faith in Christ and Baptism
By being born into a family in which both parents are Christian
By reaching the age of reason and enrolling in a local parish
questions.correct: By being born anew of water and the Spirit, through faith in Christ and Baptism

questions.question: According to the Catechism, what is the Holy Spirit to the Body of Christ, which is the Church?
questions.answer: "What the soul is to the human body, the Holy Spirit is to the Body of Christ, which is the Church." (CCC 797)
options: What the head is to the human body
What the hands are to the human body
What the soul is to the human body
What clothing is to the human body
questions.correct: What the soul is to the human body

questions.question: True or false: Because charisms come from the Holy Spirit, they are exempt from being submitted to the Church's shepherds.
questions.answer: False. "No charism is exempt from being referred and submitted to the Church's shepherds," whose office is "to test all things and hold fast to what is good." (CCC 801)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: Besides charity, which of these is a visible bond of communion that assures the unity of the pilgrim Church?
questions.answer: Above all, charity binds. The visible bonds are "profession of one faith received from the Apostles," "common celebration of divine worship," and "apostolic succession through the sacrament of Holy Orders." (CCC 815)
options: Apostolic succession through the sacrament of Holy Orders
One liturgical language used in every particular Church
Identical rites and customs in every part of the world
A single civil government for all Christian peoples
questions.correct: Apostolic succession through the sacrament of Holy Orders

questions.question: According to the Second Vatican Council, the sole Church of Christ "subsists in" what?
questions.answer: The Church of Christ "subsists in (subsistit in) the Catholic Church, which is governed by the successor of Peter and by the bishops in communion with him." (CCC 816)
options: The sum of all Christian denominations taken together as one federation
The Catholic Church, governed by the successor of Peter and the bishops in communion with him
An invisible fellowship made up only of those who truly believe
The Church as she will exist only at the end of time in heaven
questions.correct: The Catholic Church, governed by the successor of Peter and the bishops in communion with him

questions.question: True or false: Those born today into communities that separated from full communion with the Catholic Church cannot be charged with the sin of separation.
questions.answer: True. "One cannot charge with the sin of the separation those who at present are born into these communities," and the Church "accepts them with respect and affection as brothers." (CCC 818)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the Catechism call "the soul of the whole ecumenical movement"?
questions.answer: "Change of heart and holiness of life, along with public and private prayer for the unity of Christians, should be regarded as the soul of the whole ecumenical movement." (CCC 821)
options: Agreement among theologians on a single common statement of doctrine
Change of heart and holiness of life, with public and private prayer for Christian unity
The merging of all Christian communities into one organization
Shared projects of service to the poor among the different churches
questions.correct: Change of heart and holiness of life, with public and private prayer for Christian unity

questions.question: How does the Catechism describe the holiness of the Church on earth?
questions.answer: "The Church on earth is endowed already with a sanctity that is real though imperfect." In her members, "perfect holiness is something yet to be acquired." (CCC 825)
options: A sanctity that is perfect in all her members
A sanctity that is real though imperfect
A sanctity that is hoped for but not yet real
A sanctity found only in her ordained ministers
questions.correct: A sanctity that is real though imperfect

questions.question: What does the Church do when she canonizes some of the faithful?
questions.answer: Canonizing means "solemnly proclaiming that they practiced heroic virtue and lived in fidelity to God's grace"; the Church proposes the saints "as models and intercessors." (CCC 828)
options: She declares that they never committed any sin throughout their lives
She grants them a place in heaven that they did not have before
She solemnly proclaims that they practiced heroic virtue and lived in fidelity to God's grace
She makes them objects of adoration equal to that given to God
questions.correct: She solemnly proclaims that they practiced heroic virtue and lived in fidelity to God's grace

questions.question: How does the Catechism describe the Catholic Church's communion with the Orthodox Churches?
questions.answer: With the Orthodox Churches, "this communion is so profound 'that it lacks little to attain the fullness that would permit a common celebration of the Lord's Eucharist.'" (CCC 838)
options: Already complete, so that a common celebration of the Eucharist is permitted
No different from the Church's relationship with non-Christian religions
Entirely broken, so that no real communion of any kind remains
So profound that it lacks little to attain the fullness permitting a common Eucharist
questions.correct: So profound that it lacks little to attain the fullness permitting a common Eucharist

questions.question: Reformulated positively, what does "Outside the Church there is no salvation" mean?
questions.answer: "Reformulated positively, it means that all salvation comes from Christ the Head through the Church which is his Body." (CCC 846)
options: Only those whose names are on a parish register can be saved
All salvation comes from Christ the Head through the Church which is his Body
The Church herself, rather than Christ, is the source of salvation
Everyone who has not been baptized is certainly lost
questions.correct: All salvation comes from Christ the Head through the Church which is his Body

questions.question: True or false: Those who, through no fault of their own, do not know Christ or his Church, but sincerely seek God and try to do his will as known through conscience, may achieve eternal salvation.
questions.answer: True. Those who seek God "with a sincere heart, and, moved by grace, try in their actions to do his will as they know it through the dictates of their conscience—those too may achieve eternal salvation." (CCC 847)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: Whom does the Catechism call "the principal agent of the whole of the Church's mission"?
questions.answer: "The Holy Spirit is the protagonist, 'the principal agent of the whole of the Church's mission.' It is he who leads the Church on her missionary paths." (CCC 852)
options: The Pope
The missionary religious orders
The Holy Spirit
The lay faithful
questions.correct: The Holy Spirit

questions.question: Which aspect of the apostles' office cannot be transmitted to their successors?
questions.answer: "In the office of the apostles there is one aspect that cannot be transmitted: to be the chosen witnesses of the Lord's Resurrection and so the foundation stones of the Church." (CCC 860)
options: The office of shepherding the Church, which ended with the last apostle
The duty of preaching the Gospel to every nation of the world
The authority to teach in Christ's name and to guide the faithful
Being the chosen witnesses of the Lord's Resurrection and the Church's foundation stones
questions.correct: Being the chosen witnesses of the Lord's Resurrection and the Church's foundation stones

questions.question: True or false: The college of bishops has authority over the universal Church even when it is not united with the Roman Pontiff.
questions.answer: False. "The college or body of bishops has no authority unless united with the Roman Pontiff, Peter's successor, as its head." (CCC 883)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: When does the Roman Pontiff enjoy the charism of infallibility?
questions.answer: He enjoys it "when, as supreme pastor and teacher of all the faithful... he proclaims by a definitive act a doctrine pertaining to faith or morals." (CCC 891)
options: When, as supreme pastor and teacher of all the faithful, he proclaims by a definitive act a doctrine of faith or morals
Whenever he speaks publicly, on any subject, to any audience
Whenever he makes a prudential decision about Church discipline
Whenever he publishes a book as a private theologian
questions.correct: When, as supreme pastor and teacher of all the faithful, he proclaims by a definitive act a doctrine of faith or morals

questions.question: Whom does the term "laity" designate?
questions.answer: "The term 'laity' is here understood to mean all the faithful except those in Holy Orders and those who belong to a religious state approved by the Church." (CCC 897)
options: All the faithful except bishops, who alone form the hierarchy
Catholics who hold no official ministry in their parish
All the faithful except those in Holy Orders and those in a religious state approved by the Church
Baptized persons who have not yet received Confirmation
questions.correct: All the faithful except those in Holy Orders and those in a religious state approved by the Church

questions.question: What does the life consecrated to God entail for those who freely follow that call?
questions.answer: It entails "the obligation of practicing chastity in celibacy for the sake of the Kingdom, poverty and obedience," professed "within a permanent state of life recognized by the Church." (CCC 915)
options: Practicing the virtues of faith, hope, and charity
Practicing prayer, fasting, and almsgiving
Practicing silence, study, and manual labor
Practicing chastity in celibacy for the Kingdom, poverty, and obedience
questions.correct: Practicing chastity in celibacy for the Kingdom, poverty, and obedience

questions.question: What are the "three states of the Church"?
questions.answer: "Some of his disciples are pilgrims on earth. Others have died and are being purified, while still others are in glory." (CCC 954)
options: Bishops, priests, and deacons in the hierarchy
Clergy, consecrated religious, and lay faithful
Jewish believers, Gentile believers, and catechumens
Pilgrims on earth, those who have died and are being purified, and those in glory
questions.correct: Pilgrims on earth, those who have died and are being purified, and those in glory

questions.question: How does the Catechism describe the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary?
questions.answer: Mary "was taken up body and soul into heavenly glory." "The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin is a singular participation in her Son's Resurrection and an anticipation of the resurrection of other Christians." (CCC 966)
options: The moment when Mary was finally freed from the stain of original sin
A reward Mary earned by her own merits, apart from the merits of Christ
A singular participation in her Son's Resurrection and an anticipation of the resurrection of other Christians
A symbol of Mary's holiness, with no reality for her body
questions.correct: A singular participation in her Son's Resurrection and an anticipation of the resurrection of other Christians

questions.question: Which sacrament does the Catechism call "the first and chief sacrament of forgiveness of sins"?
questions.answer: "Baptism is the first and chief sacrament of forgiveness of sins because it unites us with Christ, who died for our sins and rose for our justification." (CCC 977)
options: Penance and Reconciliation
Baptism
The Eucharist
Anointing of the Sick
questions.correct: Baptism

questions.question: True or false: Baptism forgives all sins and also removes the inclination toward evil called concupiscence.
questions.answer: False. Baptism leaves nothing to efface, "yet the grace of Baptism delivers no one from all the weakness of nature." We "must still combat the movements of concupiscence." (CCC 978)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: What does the "resurrection of the flesh" in the Apostles' Creed mean?
questions.answer: It "means not only that the immortal soul will live on after death, but that even our 'mortal body' will come to life again." (CCC 990)
options: Not only that the immortal soul will live on, but that even our mortal body will come to life again
That the soul alone will live on after death, freed from the body
That the soul will be born again on earth in a new body
That only the bodies of the righteous will be raised
questions.correct: Not only that the immortal soul will live on, but that even our mortal body will come to life again

questions.question: When does each person receive eternal retribution in his immortal soul?
questions.answer: "Each man receives his eternal retribution in his immortal soul at the very moment of his death, in a particular judgment that refers his life to Christ." (CCC 1022)
options: Only at the Last Judgment at the end of time
After the soul sleeps unconscious until the last day
After passing through a series of earthly lives
At the very moment of death, in a particular judgment
questions.correct: At the very moment of death, in a particular judgment

questions.question: What does the Church call the contemplation of God in his heavenly glory?
questions.answer: Since God cannot be seen as he is unless he opens his mystery to man, "the Church calls this contemplation of God in his heavenly glory 'the beatific vision.'" (CCC 1028)
options: The communion of saints
The beatific vision
The particular judgment
The Parousia
questions.correct: The beatific vision

questions.question: Who undergo the final purification that the Church calls Purgatory?
questions.answer: "All who die in God's grace and friendship, but still imperfectly purified, are indeed assured of their eternal salvation; but after death they undergo purification." (CCC 1030)
options: Those who die in mortal sin and repent only after death
Those who die in unrepented mortal sin, for a limited time
Those who die in God's grace and friendship but still imperfectly purified
All who die without receiving the sacrament of Baptism
questions.correct: Those who die in God's grace and friendship but still imperfectly purified

questions.question: What does the Church mean by "hell"?
questions.answer: To die in mortal sin without repenting "means remaining separated from him for ever by our own free choice. This state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God and the blessed is called 'hell.'" (CCC 1033)
options: The state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God and the blessed
A temporary purification of souls before they enter heaven
The abode where the just awaited the Redeemer before Christ
A symbol of earthly suffering with no reality after death
questions.correct: The state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God and the blessed

questions.question: True or false: God predestines no one to go to hell.
questions.answer: True. "God predestines no one to go to hell; for this, a willful turning away from God (a mortal sin) is necessary, and persistence in it until the end." (CCC 1037)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: In Hebrew, the word "amen" comes from the same root as which word?
questions.answer: "In Hebrew, amen comes from the same root as the word 'believe.' This root expresses solidity, trustworthiness, faithfulness." (CCC 1062)
options: Praise
Peace
Holy
Believe
questions.correct: Believe

questions.question: What did the word "liturgy" originally mean?
questions.answer: The word "liturgy" originally meant a "public work" or a "service in the name of/on behalf of the people." In Christian tradition it means the participation of the People of God in "the work of God." (CCC 1069)
options: A sacred meal shared in memory of Christ
A private prayer offered by a priest
A public work or a service on behalf of the people
A book containing the prayers of the Mass
questions.correct: A public work or a service on behalf of the people

questions.question: According to the CCC, the sacred liturgy must be preceded by what?
questions.answer: "The sacred liturgy does not exhaust the entire activity of the Church": it "must be preceded by evangelization, faith, and conversion." (CCC 1072)
options: Fasting, almsgiving, and pilgrimage
Evangelization, faith, and conversion
Confession, penance, and absolution
Ordination, anointing, and blessing
questions.correct: Evangelization, faith, and conversion

questions.question: How does the CCC define the sacraments?
questions.answer: "The sacraments are efficacious signs of grace, instituted by Christ and entrusted to the Church, by which divine life is dispensed to us." (CCC 1131)
options: Symbolic reminders of grace, instituted by the apostles for the Church
Holy customs that only express the faith a believer already has
Rites established by the early councils to mark stages of life
Efficacious signs of grace, instituted by Christ and entrusted to the Church
questions.correct: Efficacious signs of grace, instituted by Christ and entrusted to the Church

questions.question: In the liturgy, what is the epiclesis?
questions.answer: The Epiclesis ("invocation upon") is "the intercession in which the priest begs the Father to send the Holy Spirit, the Sanctifier, so that the offerings may become the body and blood of Christ." (CCC 1105)
options: The prayer recalling the saving events of Christ's life
The prayer asking the Father to send the Holy Spirit upon the offerings
The hymn of praise that concludes the Eucharistic Prayer
The greeting of peace exchanged before Communion
questions.correct: The prayer asking the Father to send the Holy Spirit upon the offerings

questions.question: True or false: Each celebration of the liturgy repeats the Paschal mystery of Christ.
questions.answer: False. "The Paschal mystery of Christ is celebrated, not repeated. It is the celebrations that are repeated, and in each celebration there is an outpouring of the Holy Spirit that makes the unique mystery present." (CCC 1104)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: The Church teaches that the sacraments act ex opere operato. What does this mean?
questions.answer: Ex opere operato means "by the very fact of the action's being performed"; "the sacrament is not wrought by the righteousness of either the celebrant or the recipient, but by the power of God." (CCC 1128)
options: By the faith and fervor of the one who receives them
By the personal holiness of the minister who celebrates them
By the very fact of the action's being performed
By the active participation of the whole assembly
questions.correct: By the very fact of the action's being performed

questions.question: What does the ancient saying lex orandi, lex credendi express?
questions.answer: When the Church celebrates the sacraments, she confesses the faith received from the apostles: "The law of prayer is the law of faith: the Church believes as she prays." (CCC 1124)
options: The law of faith must be fully explained before anyone may pray
Each believer may pray according to his own private beliefs
The law of prayer is the law of faith: the Church believes as she prays
Church law governs public prayer but not what is believed
questions.correct: The law of prayer is the law of faith: the Church believes as she prays

questions.question: What does the CCC teach about changing the liturgy?
questions.answer: "In the liturgy, above all that of the sacraments, there is an immutable part, a part that is divinely instituted and of which the Church is the guardian, and parts that can be changed." (CCC 1205)
options: It has an immutable, divinely instituted part and parts that the Church can change
Every part of it may be adapted freely by the local community
No part of it may ever be adapted to any culture
Only the parts composed by the apostles are unchangeable
questions.correct: It has an immutable, divinely instituted part and parts that the Church can change

questions.question: The day of Christ's Resurrection is both the first day of the week and what other day, according to the CCC?
questions.answer: "The day of Christ's Resurrection is both the first day of the week, the memorial of the first day of creation, and the 'eighth day.'" (CCC 1166)
options: The seventh day of rest
The "eighth day"
The last day of creation
The day of Pentecost
questions.correct: The "eighth day"

questions.question: True or false: The Church holds all lawfully recognized liturgical rites to be of equal right and dignity.
questions.answer: True. "Holy Mother Church holds all lawfully recognized rites to be of equal right and dignity, and... she wishes to preserve them in the future and to foster them in every way." (CCC 1203)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: According to the CCC, what does the sacred image, the liturgical icon, principally represent?
questions.answer: "The sacred image, the liturgical icon, principally represents Christ. It cannot represent the invisible and incomprehensible God, but the incarnation of the Son of God has ushered in a new 'economy' of images." (CCC 1159)
options: God the Father
Christ
The Blessed Virgin Mary
The angels and saints
questions.correct: Christ

questions.question: In the typological reading of Scripture, what did the manna in the desert prefigure?
questions.answer: "The flood and Noah's ark prefigured salvation by Baptism" and "manna in the desert prefigured the Eucharist, 'the true bread from heaven.'" (CCC 1094)
options: Baptism
Confirmation
The Anointing of the Sick
The Eucharist
questions.correct: The Eucharist

questions.question: Which sacrament does the CCC call the "Sacrament of sacraments," to which all the others are ordered as to their end?
questions.answer: "The Eucharist occupies a unique place as the 'Sacrament of sacraments': 'all the other sacraments are ordered to it as to their end.'" (CCC 1211)
options: Baptism
Holy Orders
The Eucharist
Confirmation
questions.correct: The Eucharist

questions.question: Which two sacraments are called the sacraments of healing?
questions.answer: Christ willed that his Church continue his work of healing and salvation: "This is the purpose of the two sacraments of healing: the sacrament of Penance and the sacrament of Anointing of the Sick." (CCC 1421)
options: Baptism and Penance
The Eucharist and the Anointing of the Sick
Confirmation and Penance
Penance and the Anointing of the Sick
questions.correct: Penance and the Anointing of the Sick

questions.question: Which two sacraments does the CCC describe as "directed towards the salvation of others"?
questions.answer: "Two other sacraments, Holy Orders and Matrimony, are directed towards the salvation of others; if they contribute as well to personal salvation, it is through service to others that they do so." (CCC 1534)
options: Baptism and Confirmation
Penance and the Anointing of the Sick
Holy Orders and Matrimony
Confirmation and Holy Orders
questions.correct: Holy Orders and Matrimony

questions.question: What does the Greek word baptizein, from which Baptism takes its name, mean?
questions.answer: "To baptize (Greek baptizein) means to 'plunge' or 'immerse'; the 'plunge' into the water symbolizes the catechumen's burial into Christ's death, from which he rises up by resurrection with him." (CCC 1214)
options: To "plunge" or "immerse"
To "wash" or "cleanse"
To "anoint" or "seal"
To "enlighten" or "illumine"
questions.correct: To "plunge" or "immerse"

questions.question: True or false: A baptized person who later falls into grave sin must be baptized again.
questions.answer: False. Baptism seals the Christian with an indelible spiritual mark. "No sin can erase this mark... Given once for all, Baptism cannot be repeated." (CCC 1272)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: What does the Church call it when someone suffers death for the sake of the faith without having received Baptism?
questions.answer: Those "who suffer death for the sake of the faith without having received Baptism are baptized by their death for and with Christ. This Baptism of blood... brings about the fruits of Baptism without being a sacrament." (CCC 1258)
options: Baptism of desire
Conditional Baptism
Emergency Baptism
Baptism of blood
questions.correct: Baptism of blood

questions.question: According to the CCC, which of these remains in a person after Baptism?
questions.answer: By Baptism "all sins are forgiven, original sin and all personal sins, as well as all punishment for sin." Yet there remains "an inclination to sin that Tradition calls concupiscence." (CCC 1263, 1264)
options: Original sin, though in a weakened form
The guilt of personal sins committed before Baptism
An inclination to sin called concupiscence
The punishment due for sins committed before Baptism
questions.correct: An inclination to sin called concupiscence

questions.question: In case of necessity, who can baptize?
questions.answer: "In case of necessity, any person can baptize provided that he have the intention of doing that which the Church does" and pours water on the head while invoking the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. (CCC 1284)
options: Only a priest or a deacon
Any person who intends to do what the Church does
Only a Catholic who has been confirmed
Only a bishop or someone he delegates
questions.correct: Any person who intends to do what the Church does

questions.question: What does the Church do regarding children who have died without Baptism?
questions.answer: "The Church can only entrust them to the mercy of God, as she does in her funeral rites for them," and God's mercy allows "us to hope that there is a way of salvation for children who have died without Baptism." (CCC 1261)
options: She declares that they are certainly excluded from salvation
She teaches that they are saved by their parents' Baptism
She entrusts them to the mercy of God, as in her funeral rites for them
She forbids any prayer or funeral rite for them
questions.correct: She entrusts them to the mercy of God, as in her funeral rites for them

questions.question: What kind of faith is required for Baptism?
questions.answer: "The faith required for Baptism is not a perfect and mature faith, but a beginning that is called to develop." It is only within the faith of the Church that each of the faithful can believe. (CCC 1253)
options: Not a perfect and mature faith, but a beginning that is called to develop
A perfect and mature faith, tested over several years
A faith able to explain every article of the Creed
