No faith at all, since Baptism is given only to infants
questions.correct: Not a perfect and mature faith, but a beginning that is called to develop

questions.question: What do the Eastern Churches call the sacrament known in the West as Confirmation?
questions.answer: Because of the anointing with perfumed oil, "the Eastern Churches call this sacrament Chrismation, anointing with chrism, or myron which means 'chrism.'" (CCC 1289)
options: Illumination
Chrismation
Ordination
Extreme Unction
questions.correct: Chrismation

questions.question: In the Latin rite, what words accompany the anointing with chrism in Confirmation?
questions.answer: In the Latin rite, Confirmation "is conferred through the anointing with chrism on the forehead, which is done by the laying on of the hand, and through the words: 'Accipe signaculum doni Spiritus Sancti' [Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.]." (CCC 1300)
options: "Receive the Holy Spirit for the forgiveness of sins"
"Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit"
"I confirm you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit"
"May the Lord in his love and mercy help you"
questions.correct: "Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit"

questions.question: In the Latin Rite, who is the ordinary minister of Confirmation?
questions.answer: "In the Latin Rite, the ordinary minister of Confirmation is the bishop." If the need arises, the bishop may grant priests the faculty of administering it. (CCC 1313)
options: The parish priest
The deacon
The bishop
The sponsor
questions.correct: The bishop

questions.question: True or false: To receive Confirmation one must be in a state of grace.
questions.answer: True. "To receive Confirmation one must be in a state of grace. One should receive the sacrament of Penance in order to be cleansed for the gift of the Holy Spirit." (CCC 1310)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: Without Confirmation and the Eucharist, what is true of a person's Baptism?
questions.answer: "Without Confirmation and Eucharist, Baptism is certainly valid and efficacious, but Christian initiation remains incomplete." (CCC 1306)
options: It is invalid until it is completed by Confirmation
It is valid but does not yet give any grace
It must be repeated once the age of reason is reached
It is valid and efficacious, but Christian initiation remains incomplete
questions.correct: It is valid and efficacious, but Christian initiation remains incomplete

questions.question: Which three sacraments confer an indelible spiritual character and cannot be repeated?
questions.answer: "As in the case of Baptism and Confirmation... The sacrament of Holy Orders, like the other two, confers an indelible spiritual character and cannot be repeated or conferred temporarily." (CCC 1582)
options: Baptism, Confirmation, and the Eucharist
Baptism, Holy Orders, and Matrimony
Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders
Confirmation, Penance, and Holy Orders
questions.correct: Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders

questions.question: Quoting the Second Vatican Council, how does the CCC describe the Eucharist?
questions.answer: "The Eucharist is 'the source and summit of the Christian life.'" In it "is contained the whole spiritual good of the Church, namely Christ himself, our Pasch." (CCC 1324)
options: The gateway to life in the Spirit
The second plank after the shipwreck
The seal of eternal life
The source and summit of the Christian life
questions.correct: The source and summit of the Christian life

questions.question: What two great parts make up the fundamental structure of the Mass?
questions.answer: The Mass displays two great parts, the liturgy of the Word and the liturgy of the Eucharist, which "together form 'one single act of worship.'" (CCC 1346)
options: The penitential rite and the Communion rite
The Offertory and the dismissal
The Creed and the Eucharistic Prayer
The liturgy of the Word and the liturgy of the Eucharist
questions.correct: The liturgy of the Word and the liturgy of the Eucharist

questions.question: What has the Church "fittingly and properly called" the change of the whole substance of bread and wine into the Body and Blood of Christ?
questions.answer: At the consecration "there takes place a change of the whole substance of the bread into the substance of the body of Christ... This change the holy Catholic Church has fittingly and properly called transubstantiation." (CCC 1376)
options: Consubstantiation
Transfiguration
Concomitance
Transubstantiation
questions.correct: Transubstantiation

questions.question: According to the CCC, how long does the Eucharistic presence of Christ endure?
questions.answer: "The Eucharistic presence of Christ begins at the moment of the consecration and endures as long as the Eucharistic species subsist." The breaking of the bread does not divide Christ. (CCC 1377)
options: Only until the end of the Mass
Only during the moment of Communion
As long as the Eucharistic species subsist
Only while the faithful are adoring it
questions.correct: As long as the Eucharistic species subsist

questions.question: How does the CCC describe the relationship between the sacrifice of the cross and the sacrifice of the Eucharist?
questions.answer: "The sacrifice of Christ and the sacrifice of the Eucharist are one single sacrifice: 'The victim is one and the same... only the manner of offering is different.'" (CCC 1367)
options: The Mass is a new sacrifice that adds to the cross
The Mass is only a symbolic reminder of the cross
They are one single sacrifice; only the manner of offering is different
The cross was a sacrifice, while the Mass is only a meal
questions.correct: They are one single sacrifice; only the manner of offering is different

questions.question: What must anyone conscious of a grave sin do before coming to Communion?
questions.answer: St. Paul urges us to examine our conscience. "Anyone conscious of a grave sin must receive the sacrament of Reconciliation before coming to communion." (CCC 1385)
options: Receive the Anointing of the Sick
Receive the sacrament of Reconciliation
Pray the Lord's Prayer during the Mass
Fast for a full day beforehand
questions.correct: Receive the sacrament of Reconciliation

questions.question: True or false: Receiving Communion under the species of bread alone makes it possible to receive all the fruit of Eucharistic grace.
questions.answer: True. "Since Christ is sacramentally present under each of the species, communion under the species of bread alone makes it possible to receive all the fruit of Eucharistic grace." (CCC 1390)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: According to the CCC, what does Holy Communion do with regard to sin?
questions.answer: The charity the Eucharist strengthens "wipes away venial sins," and it "preserves us from future mortal sins." It "is not ordered to the forgiveness of mortal sins—that is proper to the sacrament of Reconciliation." (CCC 1394, 1395)
options: It forgives mortal sins without the need for confession
It removes original sin from those who receive it
It wipes away venial sins and preserves us from future mortal sins
It has no effect on sin, only on charity
questions.correct: It wipes away venial sins and preserves us from future mortal sins

questions.question: Why does the CCC say Eucharistic intercommunion with the ecclesial communities derived from the Reformation is not possible?
questions.answer: These communities "have not preserved the proper reality of the Eucharistic mystery in its fullness, especially because of the absence of the sacrament of Holy Orders." For this reason intercommunion with them is not possible. (CCC 1400)
options: They do not commemorate the Lord's death and resurrection in any form
They do not baptize in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
They celebrate the Lord's Supper only once a year
They have not preserved the Eucharistic mystery in its fullness, especially because of the absence of Holy Orders
questions.correct: They have not preserved the Eucharistic mystery in its fullness, especially because of the absence of Holy Orders

questions.question: The Fathers of the Church described which sacrament as "the second plank [of salvation] after the shipwreck which is the loss of grace"?
questions.answer: Penance offers those who have fallen into grave sin after Baptism a new possibility to convert. "The Fathers of the Church present this sacrament as 'the second plank [of salvation] after the shipwreck which is the loss of grace.'" (CCC 1446)
options: The sacrament of Baptism
The sacrament of Confirmation
The sacrament of Penance
The Anointing of the Sick
questions.correct: The sacrament of Penance

questions.question: According to the CCC, when is contrition called "perfect"?
questions.answer: "When it arises from a love by which God is loved above all else, contrition is called 'perfect' (contrition of charity)." If founded on other motives, it is called "imperfect." (CCC 1452, 1492)
options: When it arises from a love by which God is loved above all else
When it arises chiefly from fear of eternal punishment
When the penitent feels deep emotional sorrow
When the penitent has confessed every venial sin
questions.correct: When it arises from a love by which God is loved above all else

questions.question: According to the Church's command, how often must each of the faithful who has reached the age of discretion confess serious sins?
questions.answer: "After having attained the age of discretion, each of the faithful is bound by an obligation faithfully to confess serious sins at least once a year." (CCC 1457)
options: At least once a year
At least once a month
At least once in Lent and once in Advent
At least once every five years
questions.correct: At least once a year

questions.question: True or false: The Church requires that everyday faults (venial sins) be confessed in the sacrament of Reconciliation.
questions.answer: False. "Without being strictly necessary, confession of everyday faults (venial sins) is nevertheless strongly recommended by the Church." (CCC 1458)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: True or false: The sacramental seal, by which a priest must keep absolute secrecy about the sins confessed to him, admits of no exceptions.
questions.answer: True. Every priest who hears confessions is bound "to keep absolute secrecy regarding the sins that his penitents have confessed to him." "This secret, which admits of no exceptions, is called the 'sacramental seal.'" (CCC 1467)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What is an indulgence?
questions.answer: "An indulgence is a remission before God of the temporal punishment due to sins whose guilt has already been forgiven," gained under prescribed conditions through the action of the Church. (CCC 1471)
options: A remission of the eternal punishment due to sins not yet repented of
A forgiveness of the guilt of mortal sins without confession
A dispensation from the obligation to confess serious sins
A remission before God of the temporal punishment due to sins whose guilt has already been forgiven
questions.correct: A remission before God of the temporal punishment due to sins whose guilt has already been forgiven

questions.question: True or false: A large gathering of the faithful for a major feast or pilgrimage is in itself a case of grave necessity allowing general absolution.
questions.answer: False. "A large gathering of the faithful on the occasion of major feasts or pilgrimages does not constitute a case of grave necessity." The diocesan bishop judges whether the conditions for general absolution exist. (CCC 1483)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: Because it came to be conferred more and more exclusively on those at the point of death, the Anointing of the Sick received what name?
questions.answer: "Over the centuries the Anointing of the Sick was conferred more and more exclusively on those at the point of death. Because of this it received the name 'Extreme Unction.'" (CCC 1512)
options: Viaticum
Chrismation
Final Commendation
Extreme Unction
questions.correct: Extreme Unction

questions.question: According to the CCC, when has the fitting time to receive the Anointing of the Sick arrived?
questions.answer: It "is not a sacrament for those only who are at the point of death. Hence, as soon as anyone of the faithful begins to be in danger of death from sickness or old age, the fitting time... has certainly already arrived." (CCC 1514)
options: Only when a person is at the very point of death
Only after all hope of recovery has been lost
Whenever a person has any minor illness
As soon as one begins to be in danger of death from sickness or old age
questions.correct: As soon as one begins to be in danger of death from sickness or old age

questions.question: Who are the ministers of the Anointing of the Sick?
questions.answer: "Only priests (bishops and presbyters) are ministers of the Anointing of the Sick." The faithful should encourage the sick to call for a priest to receive this sacrament. (CCC 1516)
options: Priests and deacons
Any baptized person in an emergency
Only priests (bishops and presbyters)
Deacons and lay ministers to the sick
questions.correct: Only priests (bishops and presbyters)

questions.question: True or false: The Anointing of the Sick may be given again if, during the same illness, the person's condition becomes more serious.
questions.answer: True. "If during the same illness the person's condition becomes more serious, the sacrament may be repeated." It may also be received again in another grave illness. (CCC 1515)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: According to the Second Vatican Council, as quoted in the CCC, how is the fullness of the sacrament of Holy Orders conferred?
questions.answer: "The fullness of the sacrament of Holy Orders is conferred by episcopal consecration, that fullness namely which... is called the high priesthood, the acme (summa) of the sacred ministry." (CCC 1557)
options: By ordination to the presbyterate
By election as Pope
By ordination to the diaconate
By episcopal consecration
questions.correct: By episcopal consecration

questions.question: What is the essential rite of the sacrament of Holy Orders for all three degrees?
questions.answer: The essential rite "consists in the bishop's imposition of hands on the head of the ordinand and in the bishop's specific consecratory prayer asking God for the outpouring of the Holy Spirit." (CCC 1573)
options: The bishop's imposition of hands and his consecratory prayer
The anointing of the ordinand's hands with chrism
The handing over of the chalice and paten
The ordinand's promise of obedience to the bishop
questions.correct: The bishop's imposition of hands and his consecratory prayer

questions.question: What does the Church mean when she says that the priest acts in persona Christi Capitis?
questions.answer: "In the ecclesial service of the ordained minister, it is Christ himself who is present to his Church as Head of his Body, Shepherd of his flock, high priest of the redemptive sacrifice, Teacher of Truth." (CCC 1548)
options: He acts as a delegate elected by the community to lead it
In his ministry it is Christ himself who is present to his Church as Head of his Body
He acts in his own name by virtue of his personal holiness
He represents the Pope in each local parish
questions.correct: In his ministry it is Christ himself who is present to his Church as Head of his Body

questions.question: True or false: A validly ordained man who is discharged from the obligations of ordination becomes a layman again in the strict sense.
questions.answer: False. He can be discharged from the obligations and functions of ordination, "but he cannot become a layman again in the strict sense, because the character imprinted by ordination is for ever." (CCC 1583)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: According to the Latin tradition, who are the ministers of the sacrament of Matrimony?
questions.answer: "According to the Latin tradition, the spouses as ministers of Christ's grace mutually confer upon each other the sacrament of Matrimony by expressing their consent before the Church." (CCC 1623)
options: The spouses, who confer it on each other by expressing their consent before the Church
The priest, who confers it by giving the nuptial blessing
The bishop of the diocese, acting through the parish priest
The witnesses, who confirm the couple's consent
questions.correct: The spouses, who confer it on each other by expressing their consent before the Church

questions.question: What does the Church hold to be the indispensable element that "makes the marriage"?
questions.answer: "The Church holds the exchange of consent between the spouses to be the indispensable element that 'makes the marriage.' If consent is lacking there is no marriage." (CCC 1626)
options: The blessing given by the priest
The signing of the civil marriage license
The exchange of consent between the spouses
The celebration of the wedding Mass
questions.correct: The exchange of consent between the spouses

questions.question: When a competent Church tribunal declares the nullity of a marriage, what does this mean?
questions.answer: After examination by the competent ecclesiastical tribunal, the Church "can declare the nullity of a marriage, i.e., that the marriage never existed." (CCC 1629)
options: That a valid marriage has been dissolved by the Church
That the spouses may live apart but remain married
That the marriage was valid but not sacramental
That the marriage never existed
questions.correct: That the marriage never existed

questions.question: In the Latin Church, what is required for the validity of a marriage between a Catholic and a non-baptized person (disparity of cult)?
questions.answer: "In case of disparity of cult an express dispensation from this impediment is required for the validity of the marriage." A mixed marriage needs express permission for liceity. (CCC 1635)
options: The prior Baptism of the non-baptized party
A civil ceremony held before the church wedding
Nothing beyond the consent of the two parties
An express dispensation from this impediment
questions.correct: An express dispensation from this impediment

questions.question: Which three properties does the CCC name as essential to marriage?
questions.answer: "Unity, indissolubility, and openness to fertility are essential to marriage. Polygamy is incompatible with the unity of marriage; divorce separates what God has joined together." (CCC 1664)
options: Love, mutual attraction, and shared property
Unity, indissolubility, and openness to fertility
Fidelity, a church wedding, and a large family
Companionship, financial support, and a common home
questions.correct: Unity, indissolubility, and openness to fertility

questions.question: How do sacramentals differ from the sacraments, according to the CCC?
questions.answer: "Sacramentals do not confer the grace of the Holy Spirit in the way that the sacraments do, but by the Church's prayer, they prepare us to receive grace and dispose us to cooperate with it." (CCC 1670)
options: They do not confer grace as the sacraments do, but prepare us to receive grace
They confer the same grace as the sacraments, but in lesser measure
They were instituted directly by Christ, just like the sacraments
They work by themselves, apart from the prayer of the Church
questions.correct: They do not confer grace as the sacraments do, but prepare us to receive grace

questions.question: Who can perform a solemn or "major" exorcism?
questions.answer: "The solemn exorcism, called 'a major exorcism,' can be performed only by a priest and with the permission of the bishop." Beforehand it must be ascertained that one is dealing with the Evil One, not an illness. (CCC 1673)
options: Only a priest, with the permission of the bishop
Any baptized person with strong faith
Any deacon, without special permission
Only the Pope himself
questions.correct: Only a priest, with the permission of the bishop

questions.question: According to the CCC, what must the homily at a Christian funeral avoid?
questions.answer: The homily "must 'avoid the literary genre of funeral eulogy' and illumine the mystery of Christian death in the light of the risen Christ." (CCC 1688)
options: The literary genre of funeral eulogy
Any mention of the death of the deceased
Readings taken from the Old Testament
Any prayer for the purification of the deceased
questions.correct: The literary genre of funeral eulogy

questions.question: According to the CCC, what is the human person, endowed with a spiritual and immortal soul?
questions.answer: Endowed with "a spiritual and immortal" soul, the human person is "the only creature on earth that God has willed for its own sake." (CCC 1703)
options: One creature among many, no different in dignity from other animals
A creature willed by God chiefly for the service of the earth
The only creature on earth that God has willed for its own sake
A fallen spirit placed in a body as a punishment
questions.correct: The only creature on earth that God has willed for its own sake

questions.question: How do the Beatitudes fulfill the promises God made to the chosen people since Abraham?
questions.answer: The Beatitudes "fulfill the promises by ordering them no longer merely to the possession of a territory, but to the Kingdom of heaven." (CCC 1716)
options: By ordering them to the Kingdom of heaven
By ordering them to the possession of a territory
By ordering them to earthly prosperity and long life
By ordering them to the rebuilding of the Temple
questions.correct: By ordering them to the Kingdom of heaven

questions.question: What does the CCC teach about the natural human desire for happiness?
questions.answer: The desire for happiness "is of divine origin: God has placed it in the human heart in order to draw man to the One who alone can fulfill it." (CCC 1718)
options: It is a result of original sin and should be suppressed
It is a purely biological instinct with no relation to God
It is of divine origin, placed in the heart by God to draw man to himself
It can be completely fulfilled by earthly goods
questions.correct: It is of divine origin, placed in the heart by God to draw man to himself

questions.question: True or false: The CCC teaches that true happiness can be found in human achievements such as science, technology, and art.
questions.answer: False. True happiness is not found "in any human achievement—however beneficial it may be—such as science, technology, and art, or indeed in any creature, but in God alone." (CCC 1723)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: How does the CCC define freedom?
questions.answer: Freedom is "the power, rooted in reason and will, to act or not to act, to do this or that, and so to perform deliberate actions on one's own responsibility." (CCC 1731)
options: The right to say or do anything one wishes
The absence of every law and obligation
The power, rooted in reason and will, to act or not to act
The ability to choose evil without consequences
questions.correct: The power, rooted in reason and will, to act or not to act

questions.question: Which of the following can diminish or even nullify imputability for an action, according to the CCC?
questions.answer: Imputability "can be diminished or even nullified by ignorance, inadvertence, duress, fear, habit, inordinate attachments, and other psychological or social factors." Feigned ignorance and hardness of heart increase it. (CCC 1735, 1859)
options: Feigned ignorance and hardness of heart
Ignorance, inadvertence, duress, fear, and habit
Malice, or the deliberate choice of evil
Claimed ignorance of the principles of the moral law
questions.correct: Ignorance, inadvertence, duress, fear, and habit

questions.question: What are the three "sources" of the morality of human acts?
questions.answer: "The object, the intention, and the circumstances make up the 'sources,' or constitutive elements, of the morality of human acts." (CCC 1750)
options: The motive, the outcome, and the feelings involved
The law, the conscience, and the consequences
The intention, the result, and public opinion
The object, the intention, and the circumstances
questions.correct: The object, the intention, and the circumstances

questions.question: What role do circumstances, including consequences, play in the morality of an act?
questions.answer: Circumstances "contribute to increasing or diminishing the moral goodness or evil of human acts," but "they can make neither good nor right an action that is in itself evil." (CCC 1754)
options: They alone determine whether an act is good or evil
They can increase or diminish its goodness or evil but cannot make an evil act good
They can make an evil act right if the results are good enough
They play no part at all in moral evaluation
questions.correct: They can increase or diminish its goodness or evil but cannot make an evil act good

questions.question: What does the CCC teach about passions, or feelings, in themselves?
questions.answer: "In themselves passions are neither good nor evil. They are morally qualified only to the extent that they effectively engage reason and will." (CCC 1767)
options: They are always evil and must be eliminated
They are always good because they are natural
In themselves they are neither good nor evil
They are sinful unless they arise during prayer
questions.correct: In themselves they are neither good nor evil

questions.question: How does the CCC define conscience?
questions.answer: "Conscience is a judgment of reason whereby the human person recognizes the moral quality of a concrete act that he is going to perform, is in the process of performing, or has already completed." (CCC 1778)
options: A feeling of comfort or unease about an action
A personal opinion that creates moral truth for each individual
A fear of punishment learned in childhood
A judgment of reason recognizing the moral quality of a concrete act
questions.correct: A judgment of reason recognizing the moral quality of a concrete act

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, the education of the conscience is a lifelong task.
questions.answer: True. "The education of the conscience is a lifelong task." It "guarantees freedom and engenders peace of heart." (CCC 1784)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: Which of these is one of the rules the CCC says "apply in every case" in moral decisions?
questions.answer: Among the rules that "apply in every case": "One may never do evil so that good may result from it," along with the Golden Rule and respect for a neighbor's conscience. (CCC 1789)
options: One may do a lesser evil to obtain a greater good
One should follow the opinion of the majority
One may never do evil so that good may result from it
One may act against conscience when the law requires it
questions.correct: One may never do evil so that good may result from it

questions.question: If a person's ignorance is invincible, what does the CCC say about the evil he commits?
questions.answer: If the ignorance is invincible, "the evil committed by the person cannot be imputed to him. It remains no less an evil, a privation, a disorder." (CCC 1793)
options: It cannot be imputed to him, yet it remains an evil
It becomes morally good because he acted sincerely
It is fully imputed to him as a grave sin
It is neither good nor evil and needs no correction
questions.correct: It cannot be imputed to him, yet it remains an evil

questions.question: How does the CCC define a virtue?
questions.answer: "A virtue is an habitual and firm disposition to do the good. It allows the person not only to perform good acts, but to give the best of himself." (CCC 1803)
options: A single heroic act of goodness
An habitual and firm disposition to do the good
A pleasant feeling that accompanies good deeds
A reward God grants after death for good works
questions.correct: An habitual and firm disposition to do the good

questions.question: How does the CCC describe the origin of the theological virtues, in contrast to the moral virtues?
questions.answer: The moral virtues "are acquired by human effort," whereas the theological virtues "are infused by God into the souls of the faithful to make them capable of acting as his children." (CCC 1804, 1813)
options: They are acquired solely by repeated human effort
They are inherited naturally from one's parents
They are infused by God into the souls of the faithful
They are earned by completing religious instruction
questions.correct: They are infused by God into the souls of the faithful

questions.question: Which four virtues does the CCC call "cardinal"?
questions.answer: Four virtues "play a pivotal role and accordingly are called 'cardinal'; all the others are grouped around them. They are: prudence, justice, fortitude, and temperance." (CCC 1805)
options: Faith, hope, charity, and justice
Prudence, humility, patience, and chastity
Wisdom, understanding, counsel, and fortitude
Prudence, justice, fortitude, and temperance
questions.correct: Prudence, justice, fortitude, and temperance

questions.question: Charity is the theological virtue by which we love God above all things for his own sake, and our neighbor how?
questions.answer: "Charity is the theological virtue by which we love God above all things for his own sake, and our neighbor as ourselves for the love of God." (CCC 1822)
options: Only when the neighbor loves us in return
More than God, since we can see our neighbor
Only if the neighbor shares our faith
As ourselves, for the love of God
questions.correct: As ourselves, for the love of God

questions.question: True or false: The CCC calls charity the form of the virtues.
questions.answer: True. The practice of all the virtues is animated and inspired by charity; "it is the form of the virtues; it articulates and orders them among themselves." (CCC 1827)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: Which list gives the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit?
questions.answer: "The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit are wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord." They complete and perfect the virtues of those who receive them. (CCC 1831)
options: Charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, and faithfulness
Wisdom, understanding, counsel, prudence, knowledge, piety, and hope
Wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord
Faith, hope, charity, prudence, justice, fortitude, and temperance
questions.correct: Wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord

questions.question: In a definition quoted by the CCC, sin is described as what?
questions.answer: Sin "is an offense against reason, truth, and right conscience" and has been defined as "an utterance, a deed, or a desire contrary to the eternal law." (CCC 1849)
options: Any action that produces feelings of guilt
Only an outward deed that harms another person
An utterance, a deed, or a desire contrary to the eternal law
Any violation of the civil law of one's country
questions.correct: An utterance, a deed, or a desire contrary to the eternal law

questions.question: What is the effect of venial sin on charity?
questions.answer: "Venial sin allows charity to subsist, even though it offends and wounds it." Unlike mortal sin, it "does not deprive the sinner of sanctifying grace." (CCC 1855, 1863)
options: It destroys charity in the heart
It has no effect on charity at all
It allows charity to subsist, even though it offends and wounds it
It removes sanctifying grace but leaves charity
questions.correct: It allows charity to subsist, even though it offends and wounds it

questions.question: What three conditions must together be met for a sin to be mortal?
questions.answer: "Mortal sin is sin whose object is grave matter and which is also committed with full knowledge and deliberate consent." (CCC 1857)
options: Grave matter, public scandal, and repetition
Grave matter, full knowledge, and deliberate consent
Full knowledge, harm to others, and a bad motive
Grave matter, deliberate consent, and failure to go to confession
questions.correct: Grave matter, full knowledge, and deliberate consent

questions.question: Why are certain vices, such as pride and envy, called "capital" sins?
questions.answer: They are "called 'capital' because they engender other sins, other vices. They are pride, avarice, envy, wrath, lust, gluttony, and sloth or acedia." (CCC 1866)
options: Because they are always mortal sins
Because they engender other sins, other vices
Because they were punished by death under the Old Law
Because only a bishop can absolve them
questions.correct: Because they engender other sins, other vices

questions.question: What does the principle of subsidiarity hold?
questions.answer: Under subsidiarity, "a community of a higher order should not interfere in the internal life of a community of a lower order, depriving the latter of its functions, but rather should support it in case of need." (CCC 1883)
options: The state should take over any function it can perform more efficiently
A higher community should not interfere in a lower one's internal life, but support it in need
Lower communities must defer to higher ones in every matter
Each community should act entirely independently of all others
questions.correct: A higher community should not interfere in a lower one's internal life, but support it in need

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, if rulers enact unjust laws contrary to the moral order, such arrangements are not binding in conscience.
questions.answer: True. "If rulers were to enact unjust laws or take measures contrary to the moral order, such arrangements would not be binding in conscience." (CCC 1903)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: How does the CCC define the common good?
questions.answer: The common good is "the sum total of social conditions which allow people, either as groups or as individuals, to reach their fulfillment more fully and more easily." (CCC 1906)
options: The greatest material happiness of the greatest number
The total wealth produced by a nation in a year
The social conditions that allow people to reach their fulfillment more fully and easily
Whatever the majority of citizens votes for
questions.correct: The social conditions that allow people to reach their fulfillment more fully and easily

questions.question: Which expression of the moral law does the CCC call "the source, in God, of all law"?
questions.answer: The expressions of the moral law are "eternal law—the source, in God, of all law; natural law; revealed law... finally, civil and ecclesiastical laws." (CCC 1952)
options: The natural law
The eternal law
The civil law
The Old Law
questions.correct: The eternal law

questions.question: Why is the natural law called "natural"?
questions.answer: This law is called "natural," "not in reference to the nature of irrational beings, but because reason which decrees it properly belongs to human nature." (CCC 1955)
options: Because it refers to the nature of irrational beings
Because the reason which decrees it properly belongs to human nature
Because it is learned by observing the physical world
Because it applies only to those who are not baptized
questions.correct: Because the reason which decrees it properly belongs to human nature

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, the natural law changes substantially from one era of history to another.
questions.answer: False. "The natural law is immutable and permanent throughout the variations of history.... The rules that express it remain substantially valid." (CCC 1958)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: According to Christian tradition, what does the Old Law, though holy, spiritual, and good, not give of itself?
questions.answer: Like a tutor, the Law "shows what must be done, but does not of itself give the strength, the grace of the Spirit, to fulfill it." (CCC 1963)
options: Any knowledge of what must be done
Any teaching that endures for ever
Any preparation for faith in the Savior
The strength, the grace of the Spirit, to fulfill it
questions.correct: The strength, the grace of the Spirit, to fulfill it

questions.question: The CCC calls the New Law a law of which three things?
questions.answer: "The New Law is a law of love, a law of grace, a law of freedom." It makes us act out of the love infused by the Holy Spirit, rather than from fear. (CCC 1972, 1985)
options: Fear, ritual, and bondage
Works, merit, and reward
Love, grace, and freedom
Nature, reason, and custom
questions.correct: Love, grace, and freedom

questions.question: How does the CCC distinguish God's commandments from the evangelical counsels?
questions.answer: "The precepts are intended to remove whatever is incompatible with charity. The aim of the counsels is to remove whatever might hinder the development of charity, even if it is not contrary to it." (CCC 1973)
options: Precepts bind the clergy; counsels bind the laity
Precepts remove what is incompatible with charity; counsels remove what might hinder it
Precepts belong to the Old Law; counsels to the New Law
Precepts are optional; counsels are binding on all
questions.correct: Precepts remove what is incompatible with charity; counsels remove what might hinder it

questions.question: According to the CCC, what is justification?
questions.answer: "Justification is not only the remission of sins, but also the sanctification and renewal of the interior man." (CCC 1989)
options: Not only the remission of sins, but also sanctification and renewal of the interior man
Only the remission of sins, with no inward change
Simply the cancellation of temporal punishment
The reward given after a lifetime of good works
questions.correct: Not only the remission of sins, but also sanctification and renewal of the interior man

questions.question: How does the CCC define grace?
questions.answer: "Grace is favor, the free and undeserved help that God gives us to respond to his call to become children of God, adoptive sons, partakers of the divine nature and of eternal life." (CCC 1996)
options: A reward God owes us for our good deeds
A natural talent everyone is born with
The free and undeserved help God gives us to respond to his call
A feeling of peace that proves we are saved
questions.correct: The free and undeserved help God gives us to respond to his call

questions.question: Why does the CCC say we cannot rely on our feelings or our works to conclude that we are justified and saved?
questions.answer: "Since it belongs to the supernatural order, grace escapes our experience and cannot be known except by faith. We cannot therefore rely on our feelings or our works to conclude that we are justified and saved." (CCC 2005)
options: Grace belongs to the supernatural order and can be known only by faith
No one can ever be in a state of grace in this life
Grace can be known only through a private revelation
Only the clergy can perceive grace in a soul
questions.correct: Grace belongs to the supernatural order and can be known only by faith

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, a person can merit the initial grace of forgiveness and justification through his own good works.
questions.answer: False. "Since the initiative belongs to God in the order of grace, no one can merit the initial grace of forgiveness and justification, at the beginning of conversion." (CCC 2010)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: Who are called to the fullness of Christian life and the perfection of charity?
questions.answer: "All Christians in any state or walk of life are called to the fullness of Christian life and to the perfection of charity." (CCC 2013)
options: All Christians in any state or walk of life
Only priests and consecrated religious
Only those who take religious vows
Only those the Church has canonized
questions.correct: All Christians in any state or walk of life

questions.question: True or false: The CCC teaches that there is no holiness without renunciation and spiritual battle.
questions.answer: True. "The way of perfection passes by way of the Cross. There is no holiness without renunciation and spiritual battle." (CCC 2015)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the second precept of the Church require?
questions.answer: The second precept ("You shall confess your sins at least once a year") "ensures preparation for the Eucharist by the reception of the sacrament of reconciliation." (CCC 2042)
options: You shall confess your sins at least once a month
You shall confess your sins at least once a year
You shall receive Holy Communion every Sunday
You shall make a retreat once a year
questions.correct: You shall confess your sins at least once a year

questions.question: What does the fifth precept of the Church require of the faithful?
questions.answer: The fifth precept means "the faithful are obliged to assist with the material needs of the Church, each according to his own ability." (CCC 2043)
options: To give exactly one tenth of their income to the parish
To help provide for the material needs of the Church, each according to ability
To make a pilgrimage at least once in a lifetime
To pray the Liturgy of the Hours each day
questions.correct: To help provide for the material needs of the Church, each according to ability

questions.question: What does the word "Decalogue" literally mean?
questions.answer: "The word 'Decalogue' means literally 'ten words.'" God revealed these "ten words" to his people on the holy mountain. (CCC 2056)
options: Two tablets
Law of Moses
Book of the covenant
Ten words
questions.correct: Ten words

questions.question: How are the Ten Commandments divided between love of God and love of neighbor?
questions.answer: "The Ten Commandments state what is required in the love of God and love of neighbor. The first three concern love of God, and the other seven love of neighbor." (CCC 2067)
options: The first five concern God, the other five neighbor
The first one concerns God, the other nine neighbor
The first four concern God, the other six neighbor
The first three concern love of God, the other seven love of neighbor
questions.correct: The first three concern love of God, the other seven love of neighbor

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, the Ten Commandments oblige always and everywhere, and no one can dispense from them.
questions.answer: True. The Ten Commandments "are fundamentally immutable, and they oblige always and everywhere. No one can dispense from them." (CCC 2072)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the CCC call "the total repudiation of the Christian faith"?
questions.answer: Apostasy "is the total repudiation of the Christian faith," while heresy is the obstinate denial of a truth of faith and schism the refusal of submission to the Roman Pontiff. (CCC 2089)
options: Heresy
Schism
Agnosticism
Apostasy
questions.correct: Apostasy

questions.question: Hoping to obtain God's forgiveness without conversion and glory without merit is which sin against hope?
questions.answer: One form of presumption is when man "presumes upon God's almighty power or his mercy (hoping to obtain his forgiveness without conversion and glory without merit)." (CCC 2092)
options: Presumption
Despair
Acedia
Indifference
questions.correct: Presumption

questions.question: What is the first act of the virtue of religion?
questions.answer: "Adoration is the first act of the virtue of religion. To adore God is to acknowledge him as God, as the Creator and Savior, the Lord and Master of everything that exists." (CCC 2096)
options: Almsgiving
Adoration
Fasting
Making vows
questions.correct: Adoration

questions.question: According to the CCC, when does superstition affect even the worship offered to the true God?
questions.answer: "To attribute the efficacy of prayers or of sacramental signs to their mere external performance, apart from the interior dispositions that they demand, is to fall into superstition." (CCC 2111)
options: When the faithful ask the saints for their intercession
When sacred images are used as an aid to prayer
When the efficacy of prayers or sacramental signs is attributed to mere external performance
When the faithful begin their prayers with the Sign of the Cross
questions.correct: When the efficacy of prayers or sacramental signs is attributed to mere external performance

questions.question: What is simony?
questions.answer: "Simony is defined as the buying or selling of spiritual things." St. Peter rebuked Simon the magician, who "thought you could obtain God's gift with money!" (CCC 2121)
options: Profaning persons, places, or things consecrated to God
Putting God's goodness and power to the test
The buying or selling of spiritual things
Obstinately denying a truth of the faith
questions.correct: The buying or selling of spiritual things

questions.question: Why is the Christian veneration of sacred images not contrary to the first commandment?
questions.answer: "The honor rendered to an image passes to its prototype," and the honor paid to sacred images is a "respectful veneration," not the adoration due to God alone. (CCC 2132)
options: The images themselves possess divine power
The first commandment no longer binds Christians
The honor rendered to an image passes to the person it portrays
The images receive the adoration due to God
questions.correct: The honor rendered to an image passes to the person it portrays

questions.question: What is it called when a person makes a promise under oath with no intention of keeping it?
questions.answer: "A person commits perjury when he makes a promise under oath with no intention of keeping it, or when after promising on oath he does not keep it." (CCC 2152)
options: Blasphemy
Calumny
Simony
Perjury
questions.correct: Perjury

questions.question: Why does the CCC call Sunday the "eighth day"?
questions.answer: Because it is the "eighth day" following the sabbath, the day of the Resurrection "symbolizes the new creation ushered in by Christ's Resurrection." (CCC 2174)
options: It was the day God completed creation in Genesis
It falls eight days after the feast of Christmas
It recalls the eighth day of Jesus' life, when he was named
Following the sabbath, it symbolizes the new creation begun by Christ's Resurrection
questions.correct: Following the sabbath, it symbolizes the new creation begun by Christ's Resurrection

questions.question: According to the CCC, how can the precept of participating in Mass on a Sunday or holy day be satisfied?
questions.answer: The precept "is satisfied by assistance at a Mass which is celebrated anywhere in a Catholic rite either on the holy day or on the evening of the preceding day." (CCC 2180)
options: Only by a Mass in one's own parish church
Only by a morning Mass on the day itself
Only by a Mass celebrated by the diocesan bishop
By a Mass in a Catholic rite on the day itself or the evening before
questions.correct: By a Mass in a Catholic rite on the day itself or the evening before

questions.question: According to the CCC, to whom does the fourth commandment extend?
questions.answer: The fourth commandment "extends to the duties of pupils to teachers, employees to employers, subordinates to leaders, citizens to their country, and to those who administer or govern it." (CCC 2199)
options: Also to pupils and teachers, employees and employers, citizens and their country
Only to children and their own parents
Only to children who are still minors
Only to members of the same household
questions.correct: Also to pupils and teachers, employees and employers, citizens and their country

questions.question: What does the CCC teach about children's obedience and respect toward their parents as they grow up?
questions.answer: "Obedience toward parents ceases with the emancipation of the children; not so respect, which is always owed to them." (CCC 2217)
options: Both obedience and respect end at adulthood
Obedience is owed for life in every matter
Obedience ceases with emancipation, but respect is always owed
Respect is owed only to parents who have earned it
questions.correct: Obedience ceases with emancipation, but respect is always owed

questions.question: According to the CCC, what do submission to authority and co-responsibility for the common good make morally obligatory?
questions.answer: Submission to authority and co-responsibility for the common good "make it morally obligatory to pay taxes, to exercise the right to vote, and to defend one's country." (CCC 2240)
options: Joining a political party, running for office, and campaigning
Supporting every policy of those in power without criticism
Sending one's children to state-run schools
Paying taxes, exercising the right to vote, and defending one's country
questions.correct: Paying taxes, exercising the right to vote, and defending one's country

questions.question: Why is human life sacred, according to the CCC?
questions.answer: "Human life is sacred because from its beginning it involves the creative action of God and it remains for ever in a special relationship with the Creator, who is its sole end." (CCC 2258)
options: Society grants each person a legal right to life
It is the most complex form of biological life
Each person is useful to the community
From its beginning it involves God's creative action and remains in a special relationship with him
questions.correct: From its beginning it involves God's creative action and remains in a special relationship with him

questions.question: Why is legitimate self-defense not an exception to the prohibition against murdering the innocent?
questions.answer: "The act of self-defense can have a double effect: the preservation of one's own life; and the killing of the aggressor.... The one is intended, the other is not." (CCC 2263)
options: The aggressor has lost his human dignity
Any killing is allowed when one is afraid
The civil law permits it
Preserving one's own life is intended; the aggressor's death is not
questions.correct: Preserving one's own life is intended; the aggressor's death is not

questions.question: What canonical penalty does the Church attach to procuring a completed abortion?
questions.answer: "A person who procures a completed abortion incurs excommunication latae sententiae." The Church "does not thereby intend to restrict the scope of mercy," but makes clear the gravity of the crime. (CCC 2272)
options: A public penance of forty days
Exclusion from Church burial
No penalty beyond private counsel
Excommunication latae sententiae
questions.correct: Excommunication latae sententiae

questions.question: Why can discontinuing burdensome or disproportionate medical procedures be legitimate?
questions.answer: Refusing "over-zealous" treatment can be legitimate: "Here one does not will to cause death; one's inability to impede it is merely accepted." (CCC 2278)
options: Any means of ending suffering is permitted
The patient's life has lost its value
Doctors have authority over the patient's life
One does not will to cause death; one's inability to impede it is accepted
questions.correct: One does not will to cause death; one's inability to impede it is accepted

questions.question: True or false: The CCC teaches that we should not despair of the eternal salvation of persons who have taken their own lives.
questions.answer: True. "We should not despair of the eternal salvation of persons who have taken their own lives. By ways known to him alone, God can provide the opportunity for salutary repentance." (CCC 2283)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the CCC call "an attitude or behavior which leads another to do evil"?
questions.answer: "Scandal is an attitude or behavior which leads another to do evil. The person who gives scandal becomes his neighbor's tempter." (CCC 2284)
options: Detraction
Calumny
Rash judgment
Scandal
questions.correct: Scandal

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, the Church forbids cremation in all cases.
questions.answer: False. "The Church permits cremation, provided that it does not demonstrate a denial of faith in the resurrection of the body." (CCC 2301)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: How does the CCC, quoting tradition, describe peace?
questions.answer: "Peace is not merely the absence of war, and it is not limited to maintaining a balance of powers between adversaries.... Peace is 'the tranquillity of order.'" (CCC 2304)
options: The mere absence of war
The tranquillity of order
A balance of power between adversaries
The victory of the strongest nation
questions.correct: The tranquillity of order

questions.question: Which is one of the strict conditions the CCC lists for legitimate defense by military force?
questions.answer: The "just war" conditions include lasting, grave, and certain damage by the aggressor; other means shown ineffective; "serious prospects of success"; and no graver evils produced. (CCC 2309)
options: The war must gain territory or resources
Most citizens must approve it in a vote
There must be serious prospects of success
The enemy must belong to a different religion
questions.correct: There must be serious prospects of success

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, a soldier who carries out orders deliberately contrary to the law of nations is excused because he was obeying orders.
questions.answer: False. Such actions are crimes, "as are the orders that command such actions. Blind obedience does not suffice to excuse those who carry them out." (CCC 2313)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: How does the CCC define chastity?
questions.answer: "Chastity means the successful integration of sexuality within the person and thus the inner unity of man in his bodily and spiritual being." All the baptized are called to chastity. (CCC 2337, 2348)
options: The rejection of sexuality as something evil
A discipline required only of priests and religious
The avoidance of marriage for spiritual reasons
The successful integration of sexuality within the person
questions.correct: The successful integration of sexuality within the person

questions.question: What does the CCC teach about periodic continence, birth regulation based on self-observation and infertile periods?
questions.answer: "Periodic continence, that is, the methods of birth regulation based on self-observation and the use of infertile periods, is in conformity with the objective criteria of morality." (CCC 2370)
options: It is in conformity with the objective criteria of morality
It is forbidden like every form of birth regulation
It is morally the same as contraception
It is allowed only after the birth of several children
questions.correct: It is in conformity with the objective criteria of morality

questions.question: Between the baptized, a ratified and consummated marriage cannot be dissolved by any human power or for any reason other than what?
questions.answer: Between the baptized, "a ratified and consummated marriage cannot be dissolved by any human power or for any reason other than death." (CCC 2382)
options: Death
Civil divorce
Mutual consent of the spouses
Long separation
questions.correct: Death

questions.question: How does the CCC relate the right to private property to the universal destination of goods?
questions.answer: "The right to private property, acquired or received in a just way, does not do away with the original gift of the earth to the whole of mankind. The universal destination of goods remains primordial." (CCC 2403)
options: The right to private property is absolute and unlimited
Private property is abolished in favor of common ownership
Private property does not do away with the universal destination of goods
The universal destination applies only to unowned land
questions.correct: Private property does not do away with the universal destination of goods

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, agreement between employer and worker is enough by itself to justify morally the amount of a wage.
questions.answer: False. A just wage must allow a dignified livelihood, and "agreement between the parties is not sufficient to justify morally the amount to be received in wages." (CCC 2434)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: Which of these does the CCC list as a corporal work of mercy?
questions.answer: "Instructing, advising, consoling, comforting are spiritual works of mercy, as are forgiving.... The corporal works of mercy consist especially in feeding the hungry, sheltering the homeless, clothing the naked..." (CCC 2447)
options: Sheltering the homeless
Instructing others
Forgiving offenses
Consoling the sorrowful
questions.correct: Sheltering the homeless

questions.question: Disclosing another's faults to people who did not know them, without objectively valid reason, is which sin?
questions.answer: One is guilty "of detraction who, without objectively valid reason, discloses another's faults and failings to persons who did not know them." Calumny harms reputation "by remarks contrary to the truth." (CCC 2477)
options: Calumny
Rash judgment
Detraction
Perjury
questions.correct: Detraction

questions.question: How does the CCC define a lie?
questions.answer: "A lie consists in speaking a falsehood with the intention of deceiving." Yet "no one is bound to reveal the truth to someone who does not have the right to know it." (CCC 2482, 2489)
options: Any statement that later turns out to be false
Declining to reveal a truth to one with no right to know it
Keeping a professional secret
Speaking a falsehood with the intention of deceiving
questions.correct: Speaking a falsehood with the intention of deceiving

questions.question: True or false: According to the CCC, every offense against justice and truth entails the duty of reparation, even if its author has been forgiven.
questions.answer: True. "Every offense committed against justice and truth entails the duty of reparation, even if its author has been forgiven." (CCC 2487)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: What does the CCC, citing canon law, say about the sacramental seal?
questions.answer: "The sacramental seal is inviolable" (CIC, can. 983). Professional secrets must also be kept, and confidences prejudicial to another are not to be divulged. (CCC 2511)
options: It is inviolable
It may be broken to prevent a serious crime
It ends at the death of the penitent
It may be lifted by order of a civil court
questions.correct: It is inviolable

questions.question: True or false: The CCC teaches that concupiscence is in itself an offense, or sin.
questions.answer: False. Concupiscence "stems from the disobedience of the first sin" and, "without being in itself an offense, inclines man to commit sins." (CCC 2515)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: According to the CCC, in which three areas are the "pure in heart" attuned to the demands of God's holiness?
questions.answer: "Pure in heart" refers to those attuned to the demands of God's holiness, "chiefly in three areas: charity; chastity or sexual rectitude; love of truth and orthodoxy of faith." (CCC 2518)
options: Fasting, almsgiving, and prayer
Poverty, chastity, and obedience
Charity, chastity, and love of truth and orthodoxy of faith
Faith, hope, and courage
questions.correct: Charity, chastity, and love of truth and orthodoxy of faith

questions.question: Which capital sin refers to sadness at the sight of another's goods and the immoderate desire to acquire them?
questions.answer: "Envy is a capital sin. It refers to the sadness at the sight of another's goods and the immoderate desire to acquire them for oneself, even unjustly." (CCC 2539)
options: Envy
Avarice
Pride
Sloth
questions.correct: Envy

questions.question: How does the CCC, quoting St. John Damascene, define prayer?
questions.answer: Quoting St. John Damascene, the CCC teaches: "Prayer is the raising of one's mind and heart to God or the requesting of good things from God." (CCC 2559)
options: The recitation of approved formulas at fixed hours in obedience to the Church
An effort of concentration that empties the mind to reach inner stillness
The raising of one's mind and heart to God or the requesting of good things from God
The offering of gifts and sacrifices to win God's favor and blessing
questions.correct: The raising of one's mind and heart to God or the requesting of good things from God

questions.question: According to the CCC, what is the foundation of prayer?
questions.answer: "He who humbles himself will be exalted; humility is the foundation of prayer." Only when we acknowledge that "we do not know how to pray as we ought" are we ready to receive the gift of prayer. (CCC 2559)
options: Humility
Eloquence
A thorough knowledge of Scripture
Freedom from all sin
questions.correct: Humility

questions.question: Which Old Testament event has the Church's spiritual tradition kept as a symbol of prayer as a battle of faith and the triumph of perseverance?
questions.answer: From Jacob's night-long struggle, "the spiritual tradition of the Church has retained the symbol of prayer as a battle of faith and as the triumph of perseverance." (CCC 2573)
options: Noah building the ark while others mocked him
Daniel praying in the lions' den
Joshua circling the walls of Jericho for seven days
Jacob wrestling all night with a mysterious figure before meeting Esau
questions.correct: Jacob wrestling all night with a mysterious figure before meeting Esau

questions.question: According to the CCC, whose prayer becomes "the most striking example of intercessory prayer" in the Old Testament?
questions.answer: Once the promise begins to be fulfilled, "the prayer of Moses becomes the most striking example of intercessory prayer," fulfilled in "the one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus." (CCC 2574)
options: Jonah
Moses
Job
Isaiah
questions.correct: Moses

questions.question: Of the three parables on prayer given by St. Luke, which one concerns "the humility of the heart that prays"?
questions.answer: The third parable, "the Pharisee and the tax collector," "concerns the humility of the heart that prays. 'God, be merciful to me a sinner!'" (CCC 2613)
options: The importunate friend
The importunate widow
The Pharisee and the tax collector
The prodigal son
questions.correct: The Pharisee and the tax collector

questions.question: The CCC quotes St. Augustine's summary of the three dimensions of Jesus' prayer. Which is it?
questions.answer: St. Augustine: "He prays for us as our priest, prays in us as our Head, and is prayed to by us as our God. Therefore let us acknowledge our voice in him and his in us." (CCC 2616)
options: He prays for us as our brother, prays with us as our teacher, and is honored by us as our model
He prays for us as our prophet, prays before us as our king, and is obeyed by us as our Lord
He prays to the Father as Son, prays with the saints as our brother, and is praised by us as our teacher
He prays for us as our priest, prays in us as our Head, and is prayed to by us as our God
questions.correct: He prays for us as our priest, prays in us as our Head, and is prayed to by us as our God

questions.question: Which list gives the basic forms of prayer that the Holy Spirit inspires in the Church?
questions.answer: The Holy Spirit instructs the Church in prayer, "inspiring new expressions of the same basic forms of prayer: blessing, petition, intercession, thanksgiving, and praise." (CCC 2644)
options: Blessing, petition, intercession, thanksgiving, and praise
Vocal prayer, meditation, contemplation, adoration, and petition
Adoration, contrition, thanksgiving, and supplication
Praise, lamentation, petition, intercession, and thanksgiving
questions.correct: Blessing, petition, intercession, thanksgiving, and praise

questions.question: According to the CCC, what is "the first attitude of man acknowledging that he is a creature before his Creator"?
questions.answer: "Adoration is the first attitude of man acknowledging that he is a creature before his Creator." It is "respectful silence in the presence of the 'ever greater' God." (CCC 2628)
options: Petition
Adoration
Repentance
Thanksgiving
questions.correct: Adoration

questions.question: What does the CCC call the first movement of the prayer of petition?
questions.answer: "The first movement of the prayer of petition is asking forgiveness, like the tax collector in the parable." It is "a prerequisite for righteous and pure prayer." (CCC 2631)
options: Asking for one's daily needs
Interceding for one's family and friends
Asking for health and protection
Asking forgiveness
questions.correct: Asking forgiveness

questions.question: True or false: Christian intercession is limited to fellow believers and does not extend to persecutors.
questions.answer: "The intercession of Christians recognizes no boundaries: 'for all men, for kings and all who are in high positions,' for persecutors, for the salvation of those who reject the Gospel." (CCC 2636)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: Which form of prayer "recognizes most immediately that God is God," giving him glory simply because he is?
questions.answer: "Praise is the form of prayer which recognizes most immediately that God is God. It lauds God for his own sake and gives him glory, quite beyond what he does, but simply because HE IS." (CCC 2639)
options: Thanksgiving
Blessing
Praise
Petition
questions.correct: Praise

questions.question: True or false: The Eucharist contains and expresses all forms of prayer.
questions.answer: "The Eucharist contains and expresses all forms of prayer"; according to the traditions of East and West, it is the "sacrifice of praise." (CCC 2643)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: Which does the CCC name as sources of prayer?
questions.answer: "The Word of God, the liturgy of the Church, and the virtues of faith, hope, and charity are sources of prayer." (CCC 2662)
options: Personal feelings, private revelations, and the example of holy people
The Word of God, the liturgy of the Church, and the virtues of faith, hope, and charity
The Creed, the Ten Commandments, and the Beatitudes
Fasting, almsgiving, and pilgrimages to holy places
questions.correct: The Word of God, the liturgy of the Church, and the virtues of faith, hope, and charity

questions.question: According to the CCC, Christian prayer, whether communal or personal, has access to the Father only on what condition?
questions.answer: "There is no other way of Christian prayer than Christ." Whether communal or personal, vocal or interior, prayer "has access to the Father only if we pray 'in the name' of Jesus." (CCC 2664)
options: That we pray "in the name" of Jesus
That we pray inside a consecrated church
That we use words approved by the Church
That we first obtain the intercession of the saints
questions.correct: That we pray "in the name" of Jesus

questions.question: True or false: The Church invites us to call upon the Holy Spirit every day, especially at the beginning and the end of every important action.
questions.answer: Since the Spirit teaches us to pray by recalling Christ, "the Church invites us to call upon the Holy Spirit every day, especially at the beginning and the end of every important action." (CCC 2670)
options: True
False
questions.correct: True

questions.question: According to the CCC, how did the rosary arise in the piety of the medieval West?
questions.answer: "Medieval piety in the West developed the prayer of the rosary as a popular substitute for the Liturgy of the Hours." (CCC 2678)
options: As a replacement for the Mass in places without priests
As a prayer reserved to monks and nuns
As a way of counting the Stations of the Cross
As a popular substitute for the Liturgy of the Hours
questions.correct: As a popular substitute for the Liturgy of the Hours

questions.question: What does the CCC call "the first place of education in prayer"?
questions.answer: "The Christian family is the first place of education in prayer." Based on the sacrament of marriage, it is the "domestic church" where God's children learn to pray "as the Church." (CCC 2685)
options: The parish church
The Catholic school
The Christian family
The monastery
questions.correct: The Christian family

questions.question: Christian Tradition has retained three major expressions of prayer: vocal, meditative, and contemplative. What basic trait do they share?
questions.answer: Tradition has retained three major expressions of prayer, which "have one basic trait in common: composure of heart." (CCC 2699)
options: The use of spoken words
Composure of heart
A fixed method taught by a spiritual master
Being prayed in common with others
questions.correct: Composure of heart

questions.question: True or false: Those who practice interior prayer no longer need vocal prayer.
questions.answer: "Even interior prayer, however, cannot neglect vocal prayer." In fact "vocal prayer becomes an initial form of contemplative prayer." (CCC 2704)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: How does the CCC describe meditation, "above all"?
questions.answer: "Meditation is above all a quest. The mind seeks to understand the why and how of the Christian life, in order to adhere and respond to what the Lord is asking." (CCC 2705)
options: As a gaze of faith fixed on Jesus in silent love
As emptying the mind of all thoughts to reach inner calm
As a quest in which the mind seeks to understand the why and how of the Christian life
As the repetition of a single sacred word without reflection
questions.correct: As a quest in which the mind seeks to understand the why and how of the Christian life

questions.question: How does St. Teresa, quoted in the CCC, describe contemplative prayer?
questions.answer: St. Teresa: "Contemplative prayer [oración mental] in my opinion is nothing else than a close sharing between friends; it means taking time frequently to be alone with him who we know loves us." (CCC 2709)
options: A close sharing between friends, taking time frequently to be alone with him who we know loves us
A ladder of methods that leads the soul step by step toward visions
A careful study of the Scriptures to understand God's plan of salvation
A discipline of silence that frees the soul from every desire
questions.correct: A close sharing between friends, taking time frequently to be alone with him who we know loves us

questions.question: What does the CCC advise when distractions arise in prayer?
questions.answer: "To set about hunting down distractions would be to fall into their trap, when all that is necessary is to turn back to our heart: for a distraction reveals to us what we are attached to." (CCC 2729)
options: Hunt down each distraction and drive it out before continuing
Stop praying until the mind is calm and free
Switch to a different prayer until the distraction passes
Turn back to our heart, since a distraction reveals what we are attached to
questions.correct: Turn back to our heart, since a distraction reveals what we are attached to

questions.question: According to the CCC, what do spiritual writers mean by "acedia"?
questions.answer: Spiritual writers understand by acedia "a form of depression due to lax ascetical practice, decreasing vigilance, carelessness of heart." Presumption opens the gate to it. (CCC 2733)
options: The dryness God permits in contemplative prayer to purify the soul's faith
A form of depression due to lax ascetical practice, decreasing vigilance, and carelessness of heart
An excessive scrupulosity about every distraction that arises in prayer
A burning zeal for penance that leads to excessive fasting and vigils
questions.correct: A form of depression due to lax ascetical practice, decreasing vigilance, and carelessness of heart

questions.question: According to the CCC, who "prays without ceasing"?
questions.answer: He "prays without ceasing" "who unites prayer to works and good works to prayer. Only in this way can we consider as realizable the principle of praying without ceasing." (CCC 2745)
options: He who withdraws from all work to devote himself to prayer
He who recites the full Liturgy of the Hours each day
He who unites prayer to works and good works to prayer
He who never misses Sunday Mass or a holy day of obligation
questions.correct: He who unites prayer to works and good works to prayer

questions.question: Which text of the Lord's Prayer has the Church's liturgical tradition retained?
questions.answer: "St. Luke presents a brief text of five petitions, while St. Matthew gives a more developed version of seven petitions. The liturgical tradition of the Church has retained St. Matthew's text." (CCC 2759)
options: St. Luke's version, with five petitions
A combined text of St. Luke and St. Matthew, with six petitions
A shorter text written by the early councils, with four petitions
St. Matthew's version, with seven petitions
questions.correct: St. Matthew's version, with seven petitions

questions.question: According to the CCC, what does "who art in heaven" mean in the Lord's Prayer?
questions.answer: "This biblical expression does not mean a place ('space'), but a way of being; it does not mean that God is distant, but majestic." (CCC 2794)
options: Not a place but a way of being: God is not distant but majestic
That God dwells in a place far above the visible universe
That God stays distant from earthly affairs until the end of time
That God can be reached only after death
questions.correct: Not a place but a way of being: God is not distant but majestic

questions.question: In the Lord's Prayer, how is "to hallow" in "hallowed be thy name" understood above all?
questions.answer: The term "to hallow" is understood "not primarily in its causative sense (only God hallows, makes holy), but above all in an evaluative sense: to recognize as holy, to treat in a holy way." (CCC 2807)
options: In a causative sense: by our prayer we make God's name holy
As a vow to avoid speaking God's name aloud
In an evaluative sense: to recognize as holy, to treat in a holy way
As a blessing that we confer upon God's name
questions.correct: In an evaluative sense: to recognize as holy, to treat in a holy way

questions.question: According to the CCC, to what does "thy kingdom come" refer primarily?
questions.answer: In the Lord's Prayer, "thy kingdom come" refers primarily to "the final coming of the reign of God through Christ's return." Far from distracting the Church from her mission, "this desire commits her to it all the more strongly." (CCC 2818)
options: The growth of a just and prosperous society on earth
The final coming of the reign of God through Christ's return
The extension of the Church's authority over the nations
The arrival of each soul in heaven at the moment of death
questions.correct: The final coming of the reign of God through Christ's return

questions.question: The Greek word for "daily" (epiousios) occurs nowhere else in the New Testament. Taken literally ("super-essential"), what does it refer to?
questions.answer: "Taken literally (epi-ousios: 'super-essential'), it refers directly to the Bread of Life, the Body of Christ, the 'medicine of immortality,' without which we have no life within us." (CCC 2837)
options: The manna given to Israel in the desert
Only the ordinary food needed for one day
The Bread of Life, the Body of Christ
The bread of the Presence kept in the Temple
questions.correct: The Bread of Life, the Body of Christ

questions.question: Which petition of the Lord's Prayer is the only one the Lord returns to and develops explicitly in the Sermon on the Mount?
questions.answer: The petition for forgiveness "is so important that it is the only one to which the Lord returns and which he develops explicitly in the Sermon on the Mount." (CCC 2841)
options: "Forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us"
"Give us this day our daily bread"
"Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven"
"Lead us not into temptation"
questions.correct: "Forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us"

questions.question: True or false: Forgiving others from the heart requires that we no longer feel or remember the offense.
questions.answer: "It is not in our power not to feel or to forget an offense; but the heart that offers itself to the Holy Spirit turns injury into compassion and purifies the memory in transforming the hurt into intercession." (CCC 2843)
options: True
False
questions.correct: False

questions.question: According to the CCC, what does the Greek verb behind "lead us not into temptation" mean?
questions.answer: The Greek means both "do not allow us to enter into temptation" and "do not let us yield to temptation." For "God cannot be tempted by evil and he himself tempts no one." (CCC 2846)
options: "Do not test us," since God sometimes tempts people in order to prove them
"Remove every temptation from our lives," so that we never face a trial
"Do not punish us" for the temptations we have felt and resisted
Both "do not allow us to enter into temptation" and "do not let us yield to temptation"
questions.correct: Both "do not allow us to enter into temptation" and "do not let us yield to temptation"

questions.question: In the petition "deliver us from evil," what does "evil" refer to?
questions.answer: "In this petition, evil is not an abstraction, but refers to a person, Satan, the Evil One, the angel who opposes God." (CCC 2851)
options: An abstraction standing for every kind of misfortune
The weakness of human nature after the Fall
The suffering caused by sickness and natural disasters
A person, Satan, the Evil One, the angel who opposes God
questions.correct: A person, Satan, the Evil One, the angel who opposes God

saints.name: St. Joachim
clues: According to the ancient Protoevangelium of James, this saint's offering at the Temple was rejected because he had no children.
Tradition says he went into the wilderness to fast and pray for forty days, asking God for a child.
Tradition says an angel told him that his prayers had been answered.
His name is not found anywhere in the Bible; it comes from early Christian tradition.
He is a patron saint of fathers and grandfathers.
He shares his feast day, July 26, with his wife.
He and his wife were already old when their only child was born.
He is the grandfather of Jesus.
His wife is St. Anne.
He is the father of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
saints.invocation: Saint Joachim, pray for me!

saints.name: St. Anne
clues: In the Protoevangelium of James, this saint wept over her childlessness under a laurel tree after seeing a nest of baby sparrows.
A famous basilica shrine near Quebec City, Canada, is dedicated to her and is known for healings.
Her name comes from the Hebrew word for "grace."
She is a patron saint of grandmothers and of women in labor.
She shares her feast day, July 26, with her husband.
She is often shown in art teaching her young daughter to read.
She and her husband were already old when their only child was born.
She is the grandmother of Jesus.
Her husband was St. Joachim.
She is the mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
saints.invocation: Saint Anne, pray for me!

saints.name: St. Joseph
